AUTONOMOUS INSTITUTIONS 
Recommendation/ Observation 
1.12   The Committee feels that the establishment of BRIC and its integration of research 
institutions under the iBRIC+ framework has significantly enhanced the governance, 
collaboration, and impact of biotechnology research in India. The data provided reflects 
commendable progress in interdisciplinary research, education, biomanufacturing, and industrial 
partnerships. However, to amplify the outcomes, BRIC should scale interdisciplinary research

breakthroughs. By scaling research initiatives, refining governance mechanisms, and deepening

Recommendation/ Observation 
1.14    The Committee applauds the Department for its strategic foresight and decisive action in 
confronting AMR. Initiatives such as pioneering homegrown therapies, cataloguing priority 
pathogens, establishing AMR bio-repositories, and advancing rapid diagnostics underscore 
India’s resolve to mitigate this global health crisis. The Committee recognizes the breakthroughs 
like Nafithromycin — India’s inaugural indigenous antibiotic targeting drug- resistant 
Community-Acquired Bacterial Pneumonia. This innovation exemplifies scientific excellence and 
addresses critical vulnerabilities among high-risk groups. The Committee emphasizes the need to 
expedite the deployment of such solutions through streamlined regulatory processes, scalable 
production, and inclusive partnerships. Strengthening AMR monitoring frameworks, broadening 
investigations into pathogen prioritization and integrating diagnostics into primary healthcare 
are vital next steps.  
(Para 5.5 ibid)

1.24 The Committee extends its profound appreciation to the Department for the visionary

The development of pioneering technologies such as InoHeal, Hip Pro, Urovib, and Preztic 
reflects a laudable effort to address pressing healthcare challenges through indigenous solutions. 
However, the Committee notes with concern that a major chunk of India’s medical device 
requirements continue to be met through imports, exposing vulnerabilities in healthcare security

Department to intensify its focus on cutting-edge research and development in high-priority

design and manufacturing of advanced imaging systems, such as CT scan machines and MRI

HUMAN RESOURCE CHALLENGES 
Recommendation/ Observation 
1.36 The Committee expresses its deep concern over the acute staffing gaps plaguing the 
Department and autonomous institutions under it, condemning the systemic over-reliance on 
temporary contractual hiring to mask chronic manpower deficits. It underscores that such short-
term stopgap measures erode institutional capacity, stressing that a robust, permanent workforce 
with specialized expertise is indispensable for driving scientific advancement and maintaining 
global competitiveness. To rectify this, the Committee urgently calls for the Department to 
prioritize filling all critical positions—scientific, technical and administrative through a mission-
driven recruitment strategy. 
(Para 6.7 ibid)

CHAPTER – II 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH THE COMMITTEE DOES NOT

AUTONOMOUS INSTITUTIONS 
Recommendation/Observation 
2.1         The Committee expresses deep concern over the current state of BIBCOL and IVCOL 
and urges the Department to take immediate and decisive action for their revival. Recognizing 
their immense potential, the Committee strongly believes that both PSUs can play a pivotal role in 
strengthening and transforming India’s vaccine manufacturing ecosystem. The Committee 
recommends that the Department proactively engage with the Department of Public Enterprises 
(DPE) and persuade them to secure a revival package for both BIBCOL and IVCOL. The 
Department could explore the possibility of merger of both the units to achieve efficiency. If the 
Department succeeds in securing the revival package from DPE, the Committee recommends that 
the Department should expand BIBCOL’s current product portfolio by initiating the production of 
critical vaccines. Additionally, the Department should actively seek technical collaborations with 
reputed international organizations to enhance manufacturing capabilities and technological 
expertise. The Committee acknowledges the Department’s ongoing efforts in developing vaccines 
for Dengue, Malaria, and Chikungunya and suggests that, upon receiving necessary regulatory 
approvals, these vaccines may be manufactured at BIBCOL and IVCOL. Reviving these PSUs 
would not only contribute to ensuring affordable vaccine availability for citizens but also position 
them as key players in the global vaccine market. Once operational, these PSUs can leverage 
their infrastructure to support vaccine exports, further strengthening India’s presence in the 
international biopharmaceutical industry. 
(Para 4.8 of 388th Report) 
  
Action Taken: 
 
2.2 A revival proposal for the BIBCOL was submitted to the Department of Expenditure 
(DoE) for seeking extra funds. The Department of Expenditure (DoE), advised DBT to approach 
the Department of Public Enterprises (DPE) for a review under para 2.1 of DPE’s guidelines dated 
13.12.2021 related to the New Public Sector Enterprises (PSE) Policy for CPSEs in non-strategic 
sectors.  Accordingly, the proposal was forwarded DPE for further consideration by the 
Committee of Group of Officers (CGO) headed by the CEO of NITI Aayog including Secretary of 
the concerned Ministry for closure or privatization under the PSE Policy.  
IVCOL: At present, in line with the Government’s commitment to green growth, the Finance 
Minister announced a new scheme on Biomanufacturing and Bio-foundry in the Interim Budget 
2024–25 (Para 69), aimed at promoting environment friendly alternatives like biodegradable 
polymers, bio-plastics, biopharmaceuticals, and bio-agri-inputs. Under this scheme, the 
Department of Biotechnology (DBT), in collaboration with BIRAC, plans to establish 
Biomanufacturing Hubs across the country. IVCOL’s existing facilities may be repurposed for 
this national initiative.

KEY INITIAVES AND ACHIEVEMENTS IN HEALTHCARE AND BIOTECHNOLOGY 
Recommendation/ Observation 
2.3 The Committee acknowledges the Department’s progress in scaling the UMMID Initiative, 
including its expansion to 30 aspirational districts, establishment of30 NIDAN Kendras and 9 
training centres, and the inclusion of private healthcare institutions such as SVIMS Tirupati and 
Mahatma Gandhi Institute of Medical Sciences, Sevagram, in Phase-II. These efforts signify a 
commendable stride toward decentralizing access to advanced genetic screening and care. 
However, given the persistent challenges posed by genetic disorders - particularly in rural and 
underserved regions - the Committee urges the Department to expedite the pan-India expansion of 
the UMMID Initiative with a renewed focus on universal, time-bound screening coverage. This 
must include100% screening of all pregnant women and newborns, irrespective of their access to 
private or Government healthcare facilities. The Committee also recommends that following the 
100% screening, the Department should work upon creating a vulnerability index which would be 
helpful in assessing the susceptibility of specific demographic groups to various genetic disorders. 
(Para 5.14 ibid) 
Action Taken: 
 
2.4 The Department is grateful to the committee for appreciation. It is envisioned that  Phase-
II of the UMMID programme  will cover more than 20 States/ UTs all over India with nearly 70 
UMMID components (outreach centres in aspirational districts, NIDAN Kendras and training 
centres) being supported, which may be beneficial to more than 6 Lakhs pregnant women and 
newborns. The UMMID programme is for development of trained manpower, resources and to 
establish network in government setup within the R&D mandates as per its AoB rules of the 
Department.  After completion of the projects funded under Phase-II of the UMMID programme, 
capacity development in terms of the trained manpower and the minimal required infrastructure in 
the major hospitals will be ready in the country. Also, through this project mode implementation 
of the UMMID programme, a primary ecosystem will be in place to take it up further in the mode 
of a National Screening Program by the concerned agency in the Government. Thus, though 100% 
screening may not be possible, given the limited budget for UMMID initiative; this programme 
can pave the way for  setting up of a ‘National Screening Programme’ for genetic disorders to be 
taken up by health agencies like MoHFW or ICMR. Further, through implementation of UMMID 
initiative, sufficient R&D resources will be generated like samples of positive cases, data 
generation on approximation of percentage of genetic disorders in the areas wherein limited 
screening programs are being implemented, that will help our researchers in advancing country 
specific R&D studies on diagnostics and treatment in genetics disorders.  However, the statistical 
data on vulnerability of the population to genetic disorders and creation of vulnerability index can 
be taken up only when the Government initiatives like ‘National Screening Programme’ for 
genetic disorders to cover 100% screening is carried out. 
 
 
Recommendation/Observation

research on neurological disorders, particularly through cohort-based studies and investigator

driven projects. These initiatives are crucial in deepening our understanding of disease

(Para 5.22 ibid) 
2.6 Keeping in view the rising prevalence of neurological disorders, particularly among the

mission to comprehensively research the most prevalent neurological diseases. This mission

(Para 5.23 ibid)

Department will support targeted interdisciplinary network projects to advance research towards

Acute encephalitis.

CHAPTER-I 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE 
GOVERNMENT 
 
BUDGET ANALYSIS  
 
Recommendation/Observation 
1.1         The Committee notes with concern the sub-optimal utilization of funds under the Central 
Sector Scheme - 'Industrial Research & Development', as over half of the allocated funds remain 
unutilized as the current financial year enters its final quarter. In light of this, the Committee 
emphasizes the critical need for the Department to expedite expenditure and ensure the optimal 
deployment of resources within the remaining timeframe of the financial year. To preempt such 
inefficiencies in subsequent years, the Committee strongly advocates for the institutionalization of 
robust quarterly monitoring mechanisms.                                               (Para 2.3 of 389th Report) 
  
Action Taken: 
 
1.2 Department duly acknowledges and agrees with the Committee's observations regarding 
expenditure. It is humbly submitted that 99% of the Revised Estimates (RE) for FY 2024-25 have 
been utilized for department CRTDH, PACE & A2K+ schemes. Furthermore, the Program 
Division has planned for 100% utilization of the allocated funds for FY 2025-26 and intends to 
seek additional funds at the RE stage through supplementary provisions. It is submitted that under 
PRISM scheme, more than 99% of the budget is utilised in past five years except for FY 2023-24 
wherein nearly 80% of the budget was utilised in view of the challenges faced due to 
implementation of CNA mechanism.  Also, for FY 2023-24 Rs. 2.32 Crores was utilised against 
RE of Rs 3.0 Crores and Rs.  67.71 lakhs was booked/utilised against unspent balance available 
with CNA account of IRD scheme of DSIR from previous year. The Department also agrees with 
the Committee's recommendation for robust quarterly monitoring mechanisms. In this regard, a 
comprehensive plan has been formulated to effectively implement and oversee the same. 
 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
1.3         The Committee finds merit in the Department’s request for an additional budgetary 
allocation to the tune of ₹ 363.92 crore, over and above the provision made in B.E. 2025-26. The 
Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department may seek the requisite additional 
allocation from the Ministry of Finance at the R.E. stage.                                         (Para 2.9 ibid) 
 
  
Action Taken: 
 
1.4 Department thankfully acknowledges the Committee’s recognition towards need for an 
additional allocation to the tune of Rs. 363.92 crore over and above the provision made in B.E. 
2025-26. As per recommendations of the Committee, Department will seek additional funds from 
the Ministry of Finance at the R.E. stage to sustain its key programmes/ initiatives. 
 

 
3 
 
CENTRAL SECTOR SCHEMES 
 
Recommendation/ Observation 
1.5         The Committee expresses concern over the substantial gap between budgetary estimates 
and actual expenditures. The Committee observes that in several instances, the actual expenditure 
remains significantly lower than the budget estimates and even the revised estimates, indicating 
underutilization of allocated funds. Such underutilization may hinder the intended impact of these 
schemes and delay the realization of their objectives. The Committee, therefore, recommends that 
the Department take proactive measures to ensure effective fund utilization by addressing 
administrative bottlenecks, streamlining project approvals, and enhancing monitoring 
mechanisms. 
(Para 3.4 ibid) 
  
Action Taken: 
 
1.6 DSIR, duly and humbly acknowledges the Committee’s observations and concerns 
regarding the gap between budgetary allocations and actual expenditures. The concern over 
underutilization of funds and its potential impact on the effective implementation of schemes is 
well taken. Department has initiated several corrective measures aimed at improving fund 
utilization. These include streamlining internal processes, fast-tracking project approvals, and 
instituting stricter timelines for implementation. Additionally, robust monitoring mechanisms have 
also been put in place, including monthly and quarterly progress/ expenditure reviews at various 
levels to track progress and address bottlenecks in real-time. Department remains committed to 
ensuring optimal use of allocated resources and will continue to take proactive steps to enhance 
efficiency, accountability, and the timely realization of its programmes/projects objectives. 
 
Recommendation/ Observation 
 
1.7        The Committee appreciates the achievements made under these schemes. However, the 
Committee believes that a more robust approach is necessary to scale up these achievements and 
expand the reach of these schemes. The Department should consider increasing outreach efforts to 
encourage wider participation from start-ups, MSMEs, and research institutions, ensuring that 
more innovators benefit from these programs. 
(Para 3.5 ibid) 
  
Action Taken: 
 
1.8 The Department sincerely acknowledges the Committee’s appreciation of the progress 
made under the CRTDH, PACE, PRISM and A2K+ schemes. The suggestion to adopt a more 
robust approach to scale up the impact of these initiatives and broaden their reach is duly 
acknowledged. DSIR is undertaking focused efforts to strengthen outreach and engagement 
activities under these schemes. This includes organizing chintan shivirs, awareness drives, and 
targeted communication strategies aimed at increasing participation from start-ups, MSMEs, 
academic institutions, and research organizations. Additionally, measures are being put in place to 
simplify access, offer capacity-building support, and enhance visibility of the schemes at the 
grassroots level. 
 
1.9 The department also remains committed to expanding the reach of these schemes and 
fostering a more inclusive innovation ecosystem. Increase in budget is required for scaling up the

achievements of PRISM scheme and enhancing the outreach of PRISM scheme. Presently, there 
are only 10 outreach centers under PRISM scheme which should be increased to minimum 20 so 
that innovators from maximum number of districts & states get benefitted under PRISM scheme.

1.10  In view of CEL's strategic significance, the Committee strongly recommends that the 
Department provide consistent policy and financial support to enable CEL to overcome its current 
challenges and capitalize on growth opportunities. The Department should ensure that CEL 
receives adequate institutional backing to secure its position as a leading player in defence 
electronics, railway electronics, IT-enabled smart infrastructure, and renewable energy. The 
Committee further advises the Department to submit a detailed roadmap outlining the steps 
required to enhance CEL's operational efficiency, financial viability, and technological 
competitiveness. Strengthening CEL's capabilities will not only contribute to national self-reliance 
in critical technology sectors but also reinforce India's public sector enterprises as key drivers of 
innovation and industrial growth.  
(Para 3.22 ibid) 
  
Action Taken:

solid waste management practices for bulk waste generators. The said proposal is motivated by

II. Plastic Waste Sorting System for recycling of Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET) Materials

Department of Biotechnology, the Department of Science and Technology, the Ministry of 
Electronics and Information Technology, the Indian Agricultural Research Institute, etc. This 
duplication of research efforts leads to fragmentation of resources, inefficiencies in execution, and 
a lack of cohesive direction in national scientific pursuits. The Committee strongly recommends 
that CSIR undertake a comprehensive restructuring to optimize its research priorities, ensuring a 
sharper focus on projects that are highly critical, have a substantial impact, and align with the 
country's strategic interests. The Committee urges CSIR to realign its research portfolio by 
concentrating on areas of national importance where it can deliver unparalleled expertise and 
breakthrough innovations. Rather than engaging in research that overlaps with other institutions, 
CSIR should collaborate with relevant Ministries and research organizations to ensure synergy 
rather than redundancy. By leveraging its strengths in cutting-edge technologies, translational 
research and industrial applications, CSIR can maximize its contribution to India's scientific and 
economic development. The Committee also recommends that CSIR establish a clear roadmap to 
prioritize high-impact research, streamline its organizational structure, and enhance its role as a 
leader in addressing national challenges. A well-defined and strategic approach will not only 
enhance CSIR's efficiency but also position it as a key driver of India's scientific and technological 
advancement in critical sectors. 
(Para 4.5 ibid) 
 
Action Taken: 
 
2.10 CSIR acknowledges the Committee’s concerns regarding perceived overlaps in research 
activities with other scientific institutions. However, it is important to clarify that what may appear 
as duplication is, in many instances, a reflection of necessary convergence in addressing complex, 
multidisciplinary national challenges. Scientific research today, by its very nature, involves 
intersecting domains where coordinated efforts are essential to generate comprehensive and 
impactful outcomes. 
CSIR’s research programs are designed with a focus on translational and industrial applications, 
aiming to deliver end-to-end solutions, develop indigenous technologies, and enhance national 
self-reliance. Thus, CSIR’s mandate centers on converting knowledge into deployable 
technologies, prototypes, and processes that serve India's industry, strategic sectors, and societal 
needs. This translational emphasis distinguishes CSIR’s contributions from those of other 
organizations working in similar areas. A part of CSIR’s activities that seemingly overlap with 
other agencies (such as genome sequencing initiatives with DBT, etc.) are specifically meant to 
generate redundancy, aiming towards improving the quality and robustness of data. 
CSIR actively collaborates with other scientific ministries and agencies, including MoES, DBT, 
DST, MeitY, and ICAR, through joint initiatives, co-funded programs, and shared platforms. 
These partnerships ensure synergy and resource optimization as well as effective exchange of 
scientific knowledge among sister ministries/departments. Few of the examples about inter 
departmental/ ministerial collaboration are as below: 
 

 
12 
 
1. CSIR has been undertaking a nationally important project entitled “Indian Breast Cancer 
Genome Atlas’ in collaboration with Dept. of Biotechnology Institute -National Institute of 
Biomedical Genomics (NIBMG) Kolkata. 
  
2.  CSIR is also partnering with All India Institute of Medical Science (AIIMS), New Delhi, 
Ministry of Health & Family Welfare to work jointly for identified healthcare related research 
projects. 
  
3. CSIR has initiated a new Scheme titled Aerospace Projects of National Importance to undertake 
much needed R&D in National aerodynamic testing facilities, Civil and Military aircraft including 
electric aircraft. 
  
4. CSIR is also partnering with the Ministry of Civil Aviation to develop a National Drone 
Mission. 
  
5. CSIR is in collaboration with the Department of Space, Department of Defence (MoD) for 
various High Technology research and development for national programs. 
  
6. CSIR has entered into Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Ministry of Micro, Small 
and Medium Enterprises (MoMSME) on June 27, 2025. Both the organizations will work jointly to 
meet the needs and demands of MSMEs under the diversified areas of Science & Technology.  
  
7. CSIR is implementing mission mode projects CSIR Aroma mission and CSIR Floriculture 
Mission. The activities being undertaken under these projects are implemented in collaboration 
with Indian Council of Agricultural Research (Krishi Vigyan Kendra), Directorate of Floriculture, 
Pune and Department of Horticulture, ICAR-IARI, New Delhi across the country.  
  
8.  Under CSIR Floriculture Missions, apiculture has been integrated in collaboration with KVIC, 
wherein the Bee boxes and colonies are provided by KVIC to the clusters established by CSIR 
under these missions. Besides, CSIR is also partnering with agencies like APEDA, TRIFED, State 
Horticulture Departments, FFDC (MSME), Central and State Agriculture Universities etc. 
  
9. Under another mission mode project, which aimed at the development of genetically modified 
cotton resistant to insect pests especially Pink bollworm, CSIR collaborated with ICAR institutes 
and Punjab Agricultural University for validation of the technology in containment. 
  
10. In line with direction of the NITI Aayog, CSIR is pursuing a project under mission mode 
aimed at identification of potential sites for commercial cultivation of seaweeds across the coastal 
states and union territories of the country and their valorisation through downstream processing to 
several value added products. Earlier CSIR had worked with the Department of Fisheries, GoI and 
several state Fisheries departments for this purpose under PMMSY and other schemes. 
 
2.11 Further, in line with the Committee’s recommendations, CSIR has already been conducting 
internal reviews to sharpen its research focus through theme-based projects and a duplication 
check. Projects are chosen and evaluated through a cross-disciplinary committee of experts drawn 
from peer institutions. CSIR remains committed to continuously evolving its strategy to stay 
aligned with India’s scientific and economic goals, while reinforcing its active role in addressing 
national challenges.

Technology in respect of all the 16 recommendations/observations contained in the ‘Three 
Hundred Ninetieth Report’. The replies of the Department of Science and Technology have been 
categorized as follows:-

6.12, 6.13 and 7.6  
 Total recommendations – 14

  Para Nos.:- 2.10 and 7.4 
  Total recommendations – 02

CHAPTER-I 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE 
GOVERNMENT 
OVERALL BUDGETARY DETAILS FOR THE FINANCIAL YEAR 2024-25 (BE, RE & 
ACTUAL EXPENDITURE) AND ALLOCATION FOR THE FINANCIAL YEAR 2025-26  
Recommendation/Observation 
1.1         A significant restructuring has taken place in the funding mechanism for institutional and 
human capacity building. The previously existing three schemes under this category have been 
merged into a single entity called 'Vigyan Dhara,' which has now been allocated ₹1,425 crore for 
the upcoming year. This consolidation suggests a move towards greater efficiency in fund 
utilization and streamlined administration. While this restructuring is intended to simplify 
processes, it will be crucial to ensure that it does not lead to disruptions in existing projects. 
 
(Para 2.8 of the 390th Report) 
  
Action Taken: 
 
1.2 The merger of three schemes; into a single unified scheme “Vigyan Dhara” is aimed to 
simplify the process, provide flexibility in reappropriation of fund among the programmes 
towards greater efficiency in fund utilization and streamlined administration. The Department is 
taking adequate measures to avoid any adverse impacts of this merger. 
 
RESEARCH, DEVELOPMENT & INNOVATION FUND 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
1.3         Although the Committee acknowledges the bold initiatives undertaken by the Department 
to encourage private sector participation in cutting-edge research in deep tech and sunrise 
sectors, it also recognizes certain concerns. These include the potential risk of fund misallocation, 
the competence of fund managers in identifying suitable recipients and impactful projects, 
implications for national security, the limited rate of return on investment, the possibility of 
private entities benefiting disproportionately at the Government’s expense, and the extent to 
which the outcomes of such research will ultimately benefit the common citizen. The Committee is 
also concerned that such a substantial allocation of funds could have yielded a significant impact 
if directed towards Government institutions. Therefore, the Committee strongly recommends that 
the Department should keep these apprehensions in mind while formulating the detailed 
framework and guidelines to implement this scheme. 
(Para 3.6 ibid) 
  
Action Taken: 
 
1.4 Research, Development & Innovation:       Department appreciates the 
acknowledgement of committee for the initiative to encourage the private sector participation in 

3 
 
deep tech and sunrise sectors. Research Development, and Innovation (RDI) Scheme has been 
conceptualized to establish a corpus of ₹1 lakh crore for providing long-term financing or 
refinancing with long tenors and low or nil interest rates to encourage the private sector to scale 
up research, development and innovation in sunrise domains. As the lead ministry, the 
Department of Science and Technology (DST) convened a post-budget webinar with India’s 
leading industrialists, venture capitalists, and startup founders to gather strategic insights for the 
effective rollout of the RDI scheme in March 2025.  
The detailed framework and guidelines for implementation process is currently underway to 
operationalize the fund in a structured and impactful manner. 
 
ANUSANDHAN NATIONAL RESEARCH FOUNDATION 
 
Recommendation/ Observation 
1.5         The Committee acknowledges and appreciates the establishment of the Anusandhan 
National Research Foundation (ANRF) as a significant and progressive initiative to strengthen 
research and innovation in the country. However, the Committee is of the view that the 
Department could have demonstrated greater foresight in expediting the procedural formalities 
and operationalization of the ANRF. With better planning and timely execution, a portion of the 
allocated funds could have been effectively utilized during the financial year. The Committee, 
therefore, urges the Department to ensure a more structured and time-bound approach in the 
future to optimize the utilization of budgetary allocations, thereby facilitating the timely 
implementation of research initiatives under ANRF.  
(Para 4.5 ibid) 
  
Action Taken: 
 
1.6 Anusandhan National Research Foundation: The government has established the 
Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF) through ANRF Act of 2023. The 
Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF) has been operationalized since February 05, 
2024. The first meeting of the Governing Board (GB) of ANRF was held on 10th September, 
2024 which discussed about India’s Science and Technology landscape and redesigning of 
research and development programmes. As per the recommendation of the GB, ANRF has 
launched multiple programmes aiming to position India as global player in select key sectors, 
driving scientific advances and innovation ecosystem, and for promoting the research and 
innovation in partnership with the private sector. These include Prime Minister's Early Career 
Research Grant (PM-ECRG) to assist young researchers for initiating their research career; EV-
Mission program under MAHA (Mission for Advancement in High-impact Areas) to promote 
research & development of Electric Vehicle (EV) adoption in India; Partnerships for Accelerated 
Innovation and Research (PAIR) in line of Hub and Spoke model, as a first step towards 
fostering research across a broader range of institutions; and  Inclusivity Research Grant (IRG) 
to provide funding support to researchers belonging to the Scheduled Caste /Scheduled Tribe for 
undertaking research in frontier areas of science and engineering. 

4 
 
ANRF endeavors to take all possible measures with better planning and timely execution for the 
effective, efficient and impactful utilization of its fund.  
 
NATIONAL QUANTUM MISSION (NQM) 
Recommendation/ Observation 
1.7 The Committee notes that the ₹ 427 crores were allocated in B.E. 2024-25 which were 
significantly reduced to ₹ 86 crores and Department could spent only 64.30 per cent of the R.E. 
till 31st January, 2025. Even after such gross under-utilization of funds, ₹ 600 crores has been 
allocated for this Mission in B.E. 2025-26. The Committee enquired about the increased budget 
allocation for the National Quantum Mission (NQM) in B.E. 2025-26 and the Department 
informed that the increased allocations will play a pivotal role in expanding and scaling up 
ongoing initiatives while accelerating the development of a robust quantum technology ecosystem 
in India. A significant portion of this funding will be dedicated to strengthening the four 
established Thematic Hubs (T-Hubs), each focused on a key vertical—Quantum Computing, 
Quantum Communication, Quantum Sensing & Metrology, and Quantum Materials & Devices. 
The enhanced funding will empower these T-Hubs to fulfill their mandates effectively by: 
Technology Development, Human Resource Development, Entrepreneurship Development and 
Industry Collaborations and International Collaborations.  
(Para 5.5 ibid) 
 
1.8         The Committee acknowledges that the launch of a dedicated Mission for research in 
Quantum Technologies is a strategic and forward-looking initiative, aligning with global 
technological advancements. However, the underutilization of allocated funds raises concerns 
about the Department's commitment and operational efficiency. The Committee emphasizes the 
need for the Department to adopt a more proactive and results driven approach to ensure the 
Mission's success. Rather than merely playing catch-up to Google’s Willow and Microsoft’s 
Majorana 1, the Committee strongly recommends that the Department adopt an ambitious vision 
to position India as a global leader in Quantum Technology.  
(Para 5.6 ibid) 
  
Action Taken: 
 
1.9 The concerns of the Committee regarding the underutilization of allocated funds in 
National Quantum Mission in the previous financial year are duly noted. The Department would 
like to submit the following clarifications and forward-looking commitments: 
  
1. Initial Underutilization: 
 The year 2024–25 marked the foundational phase of the Mission, during which the 
selection and establishment of the four Thematic Hubs (T-Hubs) was carried out. 
 The time-intensive nature of establishing these hubs at premier academic 
institutions, ensuring due diligence contributed to a slower pace of fund utilization. 
2. Corrective Measures and Acceleration: 

5 
 
 Following the establishment of the T-Hubs, the Mission has now entered its 
implementation phase with clearly defined technology development targets. 
 Robust mechanisms have been instituted for monthly monitoring, milestone-based 
disbursements, and timely approvals, ensuring improved fund absorption. 
3. Strategic Vision for Global Leadership: 
 The Department supports the Committee’s view that India must not merely play 
catch-up to international players but also work toward global leadership in 
Quantum Technologies. 
 To this end, the enhanced allocation of ₹600 crores in B.E. 2025–26 will directly 
support technology development, human resource development, entrepreneurship 
and startup ecosystem and international collaborations. 
  
PERFORMANCE OF THE AUTONOMOUS INSTITUTIONS UNDER THE 
DEPARTMENT DURING 2024-25 
 
Sree Chitra Tirunal Institute for Medical Sciences & Technology (SCTIMST), 
Thiruvananthapuram 
 
Recommendation/ Observation 
1.10 The Committee commends the efforts of Sree Chitra Tirunal Institute of Medical Sciences 
and Technology (SCTIMST) in advancing biomedical technology development, fostering industry 
collaboration, and translating research into commercially viable products. The successful 
development and market launch of innovations such as the AG Chitra Tuberculosis Diagnostic 
Kit, Titanium Nitride (TiN) coated coronary stent, Automatic Contrast Injector, and Automated 
Trolley e-drive highlight the Institute’s significant contributions to the healthcare sector.  
(Para 6.6 ibid) 
 
 
1.11         Given the impact of these developments, the Committee recommends that the 
Department extend greater financial and infrastructural support to SCTIMST to further 
strengthen its research and development capabilities. Additionally, the Committee urges the 
Department to facilitate wider adoption and deployment of these indigenous technologies across 
healthcare institutions in India, ensuring affordability, accessibility, and scalability. The 
Committee also emphasizes the need for an enabling ecosystem to promote industry partnerships 
and expedite regulatory clearances, thereby accelerating the commercialization of innovative 
medical technologies for the benefit of the healthcare sector and the common citizen. 
(Para 6.7 ibid) 
 
 
Action Taken: 
 
1.12 1. There has been a 12% increase in financial allocation to SCTIMST for FY 2025-26 when 
compared to the FY 2024-25. The Department is providing necessary support for improving the 
infrastructure to strengthen the R&D capabilities of the Institute.  

6 
 
2. SCTIMST has a dedicated 'Technology Business Division' (TBD) to take care of the 
deployment of indigenous technologies developed by the research team of the Institute. TBD-
SCTIMST co-ordinates the various activities related to the commercialisation of the know-how 
and technologies developed at the Institute and liaison between the Institute and industry. The 
information about new technologies and other developments are disseminated through SCTIMST 
Website and social media handles.  
3. The products developed at the Institute are publicized through an Expression of Interest for

International Advanced Research Centre for Powder Metallurgy & New Materials (ARCI),

company has been provided with know-how for setting up a Lithium Ion Battery (LIB) 
production line.  
5. Other collaborations are ongoing to support the product development efforts of Indian 
companies/ startups operating in energy storage technologies. 
6. Efforts have been made to utilize ARCI's research capability for multiple industrial 
applications, thereby increasing the impact of available knowledge-base / developed 
technologies for multiple stakeholders.  
  
7. Research capabilities have been developed in ceramic, nanomaterials, laser processing, 
energy, and surface engineering domains has been utilized to provide technology solutions 
to industrial and strategic sectors.  Knowledge-base in aforementioned domains has been 
used to develop, demonstrate, and transfer technologies to foster self-reliance and 
sustainability through technology recipient organizations / industrial entities. 
  
 Indian Institute of Astrophysics (IIA), Bengaluru 
 
 
Recommendation/ Observation 

8 
 
 
1.16 The Committee recognizes the Indian Institute of Astrophysics (IIA) as a premier 
institution dedicated to research and development in Astronomy, Astrophysics, and Astronomy 
Instrumentation. The successful fabrication and verification of the first 1.44-meter mirror segment 
for the international Thirty Meter Telescope (TMT) at the India-TMT Optics Fabrication Facility 
is a significant achievement, demonstrating India's capability in high-precision optics and 
advanced astronomical instrumentation. 
 (Para 6.10 ibid) 
 
1.17        The Committee recommends that the Department extend continued support to IIA for the 
successful completion of India’s commitments to the TMT project and other international 
collaborations in astrophysics. Additionally, the Committee urges the Department to explore 
opportunities for further strengthening indigenous expertise in astronomical instrumentation, 
including the development of next-generation telescopes and space-based observational facilities. 
Ensuring adequate funding, infrastructure, and skilled workforce development will be crucial for 
positioning India as a global leader in cutting-edge astronomical research and technology. 
(Para 6.11 ibid) 
  
Action Taken: 
1.18 
1.  The Department is extending continued support to IIA for the successful completion of 
India’s commitments to the TMT project and other international collaborations in 
astrophysics.  
2. The TMT project has brought in the know-how of making a segmented telescope in the 
country and IIA is in the processing of building the first segmented telescope in Hanle, 
Ladakh. This segmented 3.7 m telescope with 6 mirrors or a 6.5m telescope with 18 mirrors 
to harvest and showcase all the technologies culminated in developing segmented mirrors 
for TMT project. 
3. National Large Solar Telescope: As the Kodaikanal solar observatory (KSO) is celebrating 
125 years of its operation, the scaling up of the solar studies from the ground are being 
augmented. The proposal to set up a 2-m National Large Solar Telescope is under 
consideration. This telescope will help in continuing the legacy the country has established 
as well as to train upcoming generations of scientists. This will also bring development and 
generate employment in the remote area of the country. 
4. Space program:  
(a) IIA delivered the Ultraviolet Imaging Telescope on AstroSat which is completing 10 
years of its operation in September 2025. The VELC on Aditya-L1 is operational for 
more than a year. Currently, a proposal to build a next generation UV-optical space 
telescope is in Phase-A and further steps awaited from ISRO. With the success of the 
Aditya-L1, there are efforts to start planning the next generation solar missions.  
(b) In the space sector IIA has already established MOU with many start-ups to share/extent 
its expertise in building satellites and testing including discussions with space industries 
to open up IIA facilities for critical space instruments assembly and integration. The 

9 
 
engineers and technicians who have worked on the MGK Menon Laboratory for space 
sciences on various projects are absorbed by various companies such as Dhruva, Pixxel, 
Digantara etc. 
5. IIA is extending its resource of scientific knowledge and technical expertise in the cutting-
edge technologies like space science, navigation systems, space debris mapping etc, to both 
government and private sectors (start-ups). Based on the initial experience of extending the 
IIA facilities, there appears a potential for generation of revenue from these sectors.  
 
Raman Research Institute (RRI), Bengaluru 
 
Recommendation/ Observation 
1.19 The Committee commends the Raman Research Institute (RRI) for its outstanding 
contributions to scientific research across vast spatial and temporal scales, from cosmology to 
atomic physics.  
(Para 6.12 ibid) 
 
1.20 The successful design and development of POLIX, the world's first instrument operating in 
the medium X-ray band (8 to 30 keV), and its launch onboard ISRO’s XPoSat mission on 1st 
January 2024, is a remarkable achievement in space-based X-ray astronomy. The Committee 
appreciates the Institute’s efforts in pioneering X-ray polarisation measurements, which hold 
immense potential for advancing our understanding of high-energy astrophysical phenomena. In 
light of these achievements, the Committee recommends that the Department provide continued 
support to RRI for further advancements in space-based astronomy and astrophysics. 
Strengthening collaborations with national and international agencies, investing in cutting-edge 
instrumentation, and facilitating knowledge transfer will be crucial in reinforcing India’s 
leadership in high-energy astrophysics research. The Committee also emphasizes the need for 
sustained funding, enhanced infrastructure, and skilled human resources to propel future 
discoveries and innovations in this critical domain. 
(Para 6.13 ibid) 
  
Action Taken: 
 
1.21 The Department is providing continued financial and infrastructure support to RRI for 
further advancements in space based astronomy and astrophysics. RRI’s quest to understand the 
high energy universe continues with its participation in DAKSHA, an ambitious proposal to study 
explosive events in the universe. RRI also has a dedicated program to study the early high energy 
universe - an epoch known as cosmic dawn when the first stars and galaxies formed in the 
universe- via its in-house designed and built ground based and space based high precision spectral 
radiometers. Through these research programs, RRI has built robust and fruitful research 
collaborations with multiple national and international research labs and universities. RRI has also 
contributed to the AstroSat Mission of ISRO. The POLIX instrument was built by a team 

10 
 
consisting of senior faculty members, senior engineers and bright young minds in the form of PhD 
students, visiting students and research assistants resulting in scientific and technological 
knowledge transfer to the next generation of researchers and engineers. 
 
HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT AND CAPACITY BUILDING 
Recommendation/ Observation 
 
1.22       The Committee observes that the existing provisions for capacity building and skill 
enhancement are inadequate in effectively cultivating scientific talent. To address this gap, the 
Committee strongly recommends that the Department formulate a comprehensive policy dedicated 
to capacity building programs for its staff. This policy should focus on structured training 
initiatives, skill development, and continuous learning opportunities. Additionally, the 
Department should actively explore and establish collaborations with internationally renowned 
scientific institutions to facilitate knowledge exchange, exposure to global best practices, and 
advanced research training.  
  
(Para 7.6 ibid) 
  
Action Taken: 
 
1.23 For capacity building and effectively cultivating scientific talent several efforts are being 
undertaken in the DST, which are as under: 
 For implementation of National Programme for Civil Service Capacity Building 
(NPCSCB) - Mission Karmayogi - Finalization of Annual Capacity Building Plan 
(ACBP), the department has formulated the ACBP calendar by identified level-wise 
courses (based on competencies i.e. Domain, Functional and Behavioral) on iGOT 
Karmayogi Platform. 
 Seven (07) Training Sessions  have been organized in DST under Rashtriya karmayogi 
training initiative of Capacity Building Commission to instil “Seva Bhav” in the 
officials/scientists. So, far total of 254 employees of DST have been trained under this 
initiative.  
 14 Lectures/talks were also conducted in the Department. Two immersion programme 
were also conducted for the newly recruited scientists at INST, Mohali  and WIHG, 
Dehradun. 
  Learning Hour is observed in DST on every Monday from 4:30 PM to 5:30 PM. 
 Seven (07) mandatory  courses of iGOT Karmayogi Portal have been identified in DST for 
all the officials of DST. 
A sub committee has been formed for exploring the potentiality of collaborations with 
internationally renowned scientific institutions to facilitate knowledge exchange.

2.1         The Committee emphasizes the need to ensure that administrative and procedural 
challenges do not become significant obstacles to the Department's planned activities in the long 
term. It, therefore, recommends that the Department exercise due diligence in managing its 
expenditures to guarantee optimal fund utilization for 2025-26 while ensuring the successful 
achievement of its set objectives. Furthermore, the Committee urges the Department to make 
every possible effort in the current financial year to compensate for the suboptimal performance 
recorded during 2024-25. 
 (Para 2.10 of 390th Report) 
  
Action Taken: 
 
2.2 Based on the lessons learnt in the past, the department is taking all possible efforts towards 
optimal fund utilization during 2025-26 towards smooth execution of the planned activities 
boosting the impetus of research & development in the country.  
 
HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT AND CAPACITY BUILDING 
Recommendation/Observation  
2.3       The Committee expresses deep concern over the significant number of vacancies in the 
Department, as well as in the Autonomous Institutions (AIs) under its administrative control. It is 
particularly dismayed by the persistent reliance on contractual appointments as a stopgap 
measure to address short-term manpower shortages. The Committee firmly believes that a highly 
skilled and dedicated workforce is the cornerstone of any scientific institution’s success and 
output. Therefore, it strongly recommends that the Department adopt a mission-mode approach to 
expeditiously fill all vacant positions. This will ensure the availability of a competent and stable 
workforce, essential for advancing scientific research and institutional excellence. 
(Para 7.4 ibid) 
  
Action Taken: 
 
2.4 Most of the vacancies in Group A, Group B and Group C posts of DST Secretariat, pertain 
to CSS, CSCS, CSSS and CS (OL) cadres for which the Department of Personnel & Training 

12 
 
(DOP&T) and Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) are the Cadre Controlling Authorities. This 
Department has been requesting DOP&T and MHA time and again to allocate manpower as per 
the sanctioned strength and DOP&T and MHA have been posting officials of these cadres on an 
ongoing basis. For filling up other vacant posts, recruitment processes have been initiated in this 
Department which are at various stages of recruitment.

sufficient to execute these projects. Hence, project staff are appointed on tenure and contractual 
basis for implementation of these projects. However, efforts are underway by all the AI’s to fill

who have now gone on to establish research groups on par with the best in the world. The AI’s are 
making substantial efforts and several AI’s had initiated recruitment to fill up vacant permanent 
posts following the reservation roster for permanent recruitment, which is under process.

CHAPTER-I 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY 
THE GOVERNMENT 
 
OVERALL BUDGETARY DETAILS FOR THE FINANCIAL YEAR 2024-25 (BE, RE 
& ACTUAL EXPENDITURE) AND ALLOCATION FOR THE FINANCIAL YEAR 
2025-26 
 
Recommendations/Observations  
 
1.1 The Committee observes that the Budget Estimate (BE) for 2024-25 was ₹13,042.75 
crore, but this was revised downwards substantially by 10.09% to ₹11,725.75 crore at the 
Revised Estimate (RE) stage. As of December 2024, actual expenditure stood at ₹8,296.38 
crore, a mere 71% utilisation of RE allocations. For the year 2025-26, the Department 
projected a requirement of ₹15,983.37 crore, but was allocated ₹13,416.20 crore, reflecting 
a shortfall of ₹2,567.17 crore that could impact some planned initiatives. While the increase 
in allocation over the previous year suggests continued government support for space 
activities, the reduction from the projected requirement raises concerns about the 
Department’s ability to execute all planned projects efficiently. (Para 2.2 of the 391st Report) 
 
Action Taken 
 
1.2 At the end of the FY 2024-25, the Department was able to utilise 98% of the RE 
allocations – expenditure of ₹11,518.64 crore incurred against RE allocations of ₹11,725.75 
crore.  
 
1.3 An amount of ₹13,416.20 Crore has been allocated to the Department in BE 2025-26 
against the projection of ₹15,983.37 crore. The Department has ensured that key projects / 
programmes are sufficiently funded based on the budgetary resources made available in 
2025-26. Depending on the progress of on-going missions, R&D projects and facility build-
up, the Department would approach Ministry of Finance for additional funds at RE stage and 
through the mechanism of supplementary Grants. 
 
Recommendations/Observations  
 
1.4 The Committee observes from Chart-2 & 3, for RE 2024-25, an overall utilization 
rate of 70.75% across all schemes. Space Technology, a key sector, has utilized 70.95% of its 
allocated funds while Space Sciences shows the lowest utilization rate at 46.10%, indicating 
significant underutilization. The Committee notes that Space Applications, which includes 
Earth Observation, GIS-based services, and disaster management applications, has a 
utilization rate of 73.09%. This suggests a relatively strong performance in project execution, 
particularly in satellite-based services for agriculture, urban planning, and environmental 
monitoring. INSAT Satellite Systems has seen 60.10% utilization, reflecting slower spending. 
Establishment Expenditure stands at 65.53%, pointing to stable spending on administrative 
functions, infrastructure maintenance, and research facility operations. Other Central Sector 
Expenditure, including initiatives supporting private sector participation and space-sector 
reforms, has the highest utilization at 75.76%.                                         (Para 2.7 ibid) 
 
Action Taken 
 
1.5 Department incurred expenditure of ₹11,518.64 crore against RE allocations of 
₹11,725.75 crore during FY 2024-25. (~98% of RE allocations).

1.7 The Committee observes from Charts 4 & 5 that there has been a significant 
reduction in revised allocations for 2024-25 under some of the crucial schemes of the 
Department. The Scheme- ‘Gaganyaan Programme’ India’s human spaceflight mission, 
experienced a significant budget reduction at the R.E. 2024-25 stage, from ₹1200 crore to 
₹847.35 crore, indicating a cut of ₹352.65 crore. The actual expenditure till December 2024 
stood at ₹627.05 crore, reflecting delays in hardware realisation and milestone-based 
payments. However, B.E. 2025-26 has been restored to ₹1200 crore, suggesting that higher 
spending is expected in the coming year. The Committee expressed concern over the repeated 
fund reductions and emphasised that predictable financial allocations were crucial  for 
maintaining mission timelines.                                                                             (Para 2.9 ibid) 
 
Action Taken 
 
1.8 At the end of the financial year, the Department has utilised an amount of ₹826.96 
crore under the Gaganyaan programme, which is about 98% of RE allocations. 
 
1.9 Gaganyaan Programme involves development of several new technologies such as 
Human Rated Launch Vehicle, Crew Escape System, Crew Module, Service Module, 
Environment Control & Life Support System and Human Centric Products. The budgetary 
projections and expenditure patterns have been affected by the complex technology 
development cycle involving multiple design iterations and extensive flight/ ground testing to 
meet the stringent human rating requirements. In addition to these, extrinsic factors such as 
global pandemic and disruptions in supply chain of semiconductors & raw materials have 
also impacted the programme in recent past. 
 

4 
 
1.10 As ISRO is preparing for the first 4nscrewed mission after the completion of some of 
the major ground qualification tests, there is greater clarity on the overall outlay plan and 
yearly budgetary requirements. This is expected to result in higher expenditure in the coming 
years for flight hardware realisation and mission related activities. Further, expenditure 
monitoring through regular reviews is being carried out. Based on this cash-flow assessment, 
the BE 2025-26 provision for the programme is restored to ₹1200.00 crore.

1.55 Under the aegis of Indian Space Policy-2023, ISRO/DoS has implemented ‘Earth 
Observation (EO) Data Dissemination Guidelines’ on 22nd November 2023. Under the EO 
Data Dissemination Guidelines, ISRO is providing ‘Free and Open’ access to Indian Remote 
Sensing Data & products to all the users including academic institutions start-ups and 
industries. All the remote sensing data acquired by ISRO through its ground stations in India 
and abroad since 1988, having spatial resolution 5m & coarser, is made accessible on ‘free 
and open’ basis to all. The data of resolution finer than 5m resolution is available free of cost 
to Government entities, and at a fair pricing to non-governmental entities.  
 
1.56 ISRO/DoS is making continuous efforts in developing advanced EO based solutions 
for automatic crop mapping, monitoring crop health and crop yield/production forecasting. 

12 
 
ISRO/DoS has developed and transferred the methodology to Mahalanobis National Crop 
Forecast Centre for operational, in-season mapping of 10 major crops. ISRO has developed a 
processor called “SASYA” (Satellite-based crop mapping System with Automl) for mapping 
crops using time series SAR data through automatic Machine Learning (ML) algorithms. 
Attempts are ongoing to update the processor to map other Kharif crops.  
 
1.57 ISRO has developed algorithm for Surface Soil Moisture (SSM, @500m, 17-day 
repetivity) product generation using EOS-04 (RISAT-1A) data and the operational products 
are released through Bhoonidhi portal since December 2023. These SSM product are useful 
for drought assessment, irrigation monitoring, land hydrological modelling etc. ISRO also 
plans to enhance the temporal/spatial resolution of SSM product utilizing SAR data from 
upcoming NISAR satellite. The concurrent SAR data from EOS-04 and NISAR missions is 
expected to increase the efficacy as well as resolution of SSM products.  
 
1.58 ISRO has developed and tested GNSS-Reflectometry payload onboard EOS-
08/Microsat-2C (launched on 16th August 2024). The payload utilizes signals from GNSS 
satellites as signal-of-opportunity to map the earth surface including oceans. The data from 
this payload was processed and evaluated to assess its potential for soil moisture retrieval. 
Soil moisture retrievals from Microsat-2C correlated well with incidence of high rainfall and 
irrigation areas, demonstrating promising potential for future utilization. ISRO is exploring 
possibility of operating constellation of this payload to enhance the temporal and spatial 
coverage of the GNSS-R data and soil moisture products derived from it. 
 
1.59 ISRO/DoS has prepared the National level hydrological modelling framework under 
National Hydrology Project to facilitate dynamic computation of water balance components. 
ISRO provides daily products on surface runoff, evapotranspiration, soil moisture as 
operational outcome of the project. ISRO has also developed a web-based interactive 
hydrological modeling system to help user to build, execute and store the model results 
online, to reduce user’s dependence on software and computational infrastructure. ISRO is 
also making efforts towards developing techniques for assimilation of Indian EO data in 
hydrological models for improving the model performance. 
 
1.60 ISRO is acting as Mentor Institute for Technology Rollout (MITR) under Yield

of Krishi-DSS to support assessment and monitoring of droughts and their potential impact

for users having larger data requirements. It is also planned to include AI/ML solutions in 
Bhuvan and Bhoonidhi portals.
