9. Mass Employment Generation through S&T (MEGSAT) can be an important programme under which training is
 imparted to various identified trades with the help of S&T experts and institutions for creating technical manpower. The
 programme also aims at generating jobs on a sustainable basis. In the year 1993-94 a sum of Rs. 3.50 crores was
 provided for this programme but in the budget estimates for the year 1994-95 the allocation has been reduced to only
 Rs. 50 lakhs. The Committee wanted to know the reasons for this drastic reduction in the allocation for this programme.
 The Committee was informed that the MEGSAT programme was discussed by the Department of Science and
 Technology with the Planning Commission and it was decided that any new employment generation programme like
 MEGSAT needs to be integrated with the existing employment generation programmes like TRYSEM, IRDP, JRY, run
 by the Ministry of Rural Development. Recognising the fact that by the application of science and technology skills can
 be improved, the Department of Science and Technology should co- ordinate its activities with the Ministry of Rural
 Development and other Departments so as to explore the possibilities of employment generation particularly for the
 rural youth, women and weaker sections of society by providing greater S&T inputs into the existing employment
 generation programmes.
              
10.Under the head 'Drugs an Pharmaceuticals Research' in the budget estimates for the year 1994-95, a provision of Rs.
 10 crores has been made, but the Committee found that there         was no allocation made under this head last year. The
 Committee, therefore, wanted to know why this allocation has been made in the budget estimates for this year. The
 Committee was informed that the Department of Science and Technology is giving emphasis on the support of        
 Life Science activities along with the Department of Biotechnology and the Council of Scientific           and Industrial
 Research. According to the Department, due to the emerging global scenario, it would be necessary for the country to
 prepare itself in a big way by stepping up capabilities for indigenous drug design and development. For achieving this
 purpose, a provision for Rs. 10 crores has been made in the budget estimates for this year. The Committee was also
 informed that a committee consisting of Secretary, Department of Science and Technology, Secretary, Department of
 Biotechnology and Director-General, CSIR would guide the activities in this area. One or more of the important
 national institutions like the laboratories of CSIR and industries would also be involved in this programme. The
 Committee is concerned that when major institutions and infrastructure in this area exists in CSIR, DBT and ICMR
 why Department of Science and Technology should get involved. Any capabilities under DST which are marginal at
 present should be made available to these agencies. DST should concentrate on areas where serious gaps exist on the
 S&T scene. The Department may also made efforts to attract industry to work in developing drugs and pharmaceuticals
 from basic research to product.
 
11. The Committee observed that in the budget estimates for the year 1994-95 for the Technology Information
 Forecasting and Assessment Council (TIFAC), a sum of Rs. 7.16 crores has been allocated while in the revised

 estimates for the year 1993-94, this Council got Rs. 3.99 crores. In view of this increased allocation for TIFAC, the

 have been formulated in the form of multi-institutional projects. Further, at the instance of Planning Commission,
 specific home-grown technologies are beige supported and it is proposed to strengthen this activity during the year

 assessment and technology forecasting. If the role of TIFAC is widened, there is a possibility that it may lose its
 original direction and may start functioning as a project manager; in particular, the Committee noted in this regard the
 project management role of TIFAC in the project on advanced composites. The Committee is of the view that TIFAC
 can make a great impact in promoting science if it clearly follows its original objectives. The Committee feels that,
 being the nodal agency for promoting S&T, the Department of Science and Technology should bring about flexibility
 in the operation of the scientific departments and that there should be transparency in t operation of TIFAC. The
 Committee noted that funds allocated for TIFAC were far great than support provided to many major aided institutions.
 
12.  Societal programmes of the Department of Science and Technology aim at providing
the benefit of science and technologies directly to the people. The Committee has, however observed that in regard to
 some of the society-related programmes there are other institution which too are looking after similar types of
 programmes. In order to avoid duplication  supporting such programmes the Committee is of the view that the
 Department of Science and Technology may consider transferring some of the programmes to the specialise      
 institutions or concerned bodies, and the money thus saved can be utilized for promoting other thrust areas of the
 Department. The Committee strongly supports the S&T programme       undertaken by the Department because it is
 interested in having a very strong S&T base for the country but it would like to point out that the Department should
 regroup its activities or shed some of its load so as to concentrate on thrust areas that are not being dealt with by    
 other agencies.
 
13. The Department should also promote indigenous technologies which exist in the country which are highly useful
 and very cheap. By strengthening this area the Department would not only create Societal impact but would also be
 able to generate employment. The Department of Science and Technology should make efforts to create a strong
 technological base in the country relying on its technological traditions. The Department should investigate areas where
 India had a strong technological base and replace and upgrade some of the old technologies so that with less investment
 India can gain competitive technological edge over other countries.
 
14. Through science and society programme, the Department of Science and Technology makes the use of S&T for
 societal development, which particularly aims at influencing the lives        of weaker sections, tribals and women. The
 other component of this programme relates to the popularisation of science and entrepreneurship development .   
 through the intervention of S&T. The Committee was given an account of the activity undertaken by the Department
 during the last year and a recent successful experiment conducted by the department in this area was the Children’s
 Science Congress which was every popular among children.  The Department is also thinking of setting up of a
 National Children’s Science Academy. The Committee feels that
many of the ills which beset Indian society today are largely due to the unscientific attitude. Creating scientific temper
 among masses is, therefore, a great responsibility of the Department of Science and Technology. This is an area of great
 importance.

5. The Committee noticed that for the Mission Mode on Cyclone Warning  and Seismic Observation in the budget
 estimates for the year 1994-95, there is only a marginal increase of Rs.  15 lakh over the last year's budget estimates.
 The Committee, therefore, wanted to know whether with this meager increase the Department would be able to run this
 programme in Mission Mode, particularly when the Department intends of re-orient its approach after the earthquake in
 the Marathwada region. The Committee was told that under the Mission Mode Project, a sum of Rs. 2 crores has been
 provided in this years budget against Rs. 1.85 crores provided last year. While this Mission Mode Project will be with a
 specific intention of enhancing the capabilities of seismic observations, there is also a provision of Rs. I crore under
 seismicity. Thus total provision under seismology for the year 1994-95 comes to Rs. 3 crores. IMD also incurs some
 expenditure on seismology in maintaining its national network. The Committee was informed that as a post-budgetary
 development, a World Bank loan of 7.5 million US dollars for improving the seismic monitoring set-up in peninsular
 India has been approved. The Department also intends to strengthen its seismic network in the Himalayas and the
 North-Eastern Region. It intends to initiate the programme of micro-zoning of selected cities and locations in the
 country as this would lead to reduction of loss of life and damage to property. The Committee observes that the whole
 area of seismicity has two aspects: one relates to seismology and the other to the disaster mitigation efforts. In the area
 of seismology, the Department should upgrade - its technology. The instruments which are awfilable to the Department
 for observing seismological activities have to be upgraded as also the manner in which the data is processed and
 analysis made. The Department should also spend a part of its funds in imparting knowledge to the people as to how
 they can cope with the disaster and how the loss of life and damage to property can be minimized. The Committee feels
 that some major efforts are required to be made by the Department in the area of earthquake prediction like the
 Department has done in the case of Cyclone warnings and there is tremendous need for software development. The
 Committee is of the view that the Department needs to evolve an  integrated disaster prediction and mitigation
 programme for the entire country.
 
16. The Committee was informed that under the instrument development programme, the Department aims at planning,
 co-ordinating and implementing programmes leading to indigenous development and production of instruments. The
 allocation made for the instruments development in the budget estimates for the year 1994-95 is Rs. 2 crores. The
 Department is also making an attempt to get some part of the funding from industry. The Committee agrees with the
 Department that it is a very vital area for modernising the industry in the country and needs adequate financial support.
 
  17.       The Committee wanted to know the reasons for increase from the revised estimates of Rs. 45 lakhs for the year
 1993-94 to Rs. 1.20 crores in the budget estimates for the year 1994-95 in the area of National Coordination of Testing
 and Calibration Facilities (NCTCF). It was explained to the Committee that the increase in the provision has been made
 with a view to developing and establishing a national accreditation and wants to initiate new system of accreditation in
 order to promote our exports. The Committee felt that there was need for an integrated look at the areas of standards
 quality control, reliability evaluation, accreditation of facilities, national testing capabilities, etc. There were widely
 disparate investments in different areas, for example, Department of Electronics, Department of Science and
 Technology, etc. These need to be reviewed. A strong programme in this area is called for with the thrust on exports
 and global competitiveness.
 
18. The Committee is of the view that Science and Society programmes, Seismicity, Instrument Development and the
 National Coordination of Testing and Calibration Facilities are vital areas which require to be strengthened and,
 therefore, recommends that at the time of doing mid-term appraisal of the Eighth Five Year Plan, the Government may
 consider enhancing the allocation for these four programmes suitably.
 
19. The Committee noted the vital role that the Department of Science and Technology plays in the matter of bilateral
 and multilateral international cooperation and in particular, successful programmes that have been embarked upon with
 the former Soviet Union (now Russia and the new initiatives with the other Republics), Germany and the USA.
 
20. The Committee noticed that in the area of policy formulation anti related aspects for the science sector much
 headway has not been made but the Committee noted that the Government has recently constituted the Cabinet
 Committee on Science and Technology and hopes that it will start functioning soon and the matters pertaining to the
 setting up of Science Advisory Council to the Cabinet Committee on Science and Technology, Statement of
 Technology policy or a science and technology approach to the post GATT period would receive its prompt attention as
 these measures are vital from the viewpoint of our national development.

NATIONAL LABORATORIES
Recommendation
The Committee appreciates the Department for carrying out research in many frontier areas of science and technology.  It
 notes with satisfaction the laudable claim of the CSIR that science is one of the areas, which can bring leadership and meet the kind
 of objectives that India has set for itself.  However, it is of opinion that the Department should make efforts to raise funds from
 Industry by successful transfer of technologies.  There is also a need for wider dissemination of technologies so that there is a greater
 interface between Industry & R&D laboratories
(Para 21)
Action Taken by the Department
Department at the outset is thankful for the encourging remarks and appreciation received from the Parliamentary Standing
 Committee.  The Committee is informed that CSIR laboratories periodically organises lab-industry get together. Department also
 shares the concern of the Committee as how to raise further funds from industry through transfer of technologies. CSIR would like to
 apprise the Committee that in order to address the issue, CSIR Society, had constituted a Committee under the Chairmanship of Shri
 H.S. Singhania an eminent industrialist for suggesting further measures for enhancing CSIR – industry interface. Several suggestions
 to deepen CSIR-industry interaction now has been made by the Committee. The Recommendation interalia include stronger customer
 orientation, customisation of products and services, shifting to relationship models of business, exchange of business management
 personnel from laboratory to industry and vice-versa etc. The Recommendation of the Committee is being processed for their
 acceptance and these would be implemented.
In addition to above the department through its Public Sector Enterprise, National Research Development Corporation
 (NRDC) generates revenues by transferring/licensing technologies to industry assigned to it by R&D laboratories and other sources.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and hopes that the Recommendation of the Committee constituted by CSIR Society would be
 accepted and implemented for augmenting CSIR- Industry interface.
 
NATIONAL S&T HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT
Recommendation
The Committee reiterates its earlier recommendation made in 86
th Report that there is a need for reviewing and
 strengthening/revamping the existing S&T support systems in the universities and other educational institutions.  The Committee is
 of the view that an agreement be reached with various financial institutions for providing loans to those research scholars for setting
 up their own enterprises.
 (Para 25)
Action Taken by the Department
During the Tenth Plan, CSIR has initiated a new activity titled as Entrepreneurship support to Research Scholars, under HRD
 scheme.  The basic aim of initiation of this activity is to inculcate the spirit of entrepreneuriship into young talented scholars.  Its
 implementation would not only enable scholars to complete doctoral programme but also help them in making use of this knowledge
 by establishing linkages with those industry which requires technological knowledge as a base and thus realise value through such
 joint efforts.  The success gained by them could encourage them to setup their own enterprises. The proposal is being processed for
 consideration by the Government during the year.
The Department of Science and Technology has been implementing a programme called ‘Fund Improvement of S&T
 Infrastructure in Universities and higher Educational Institutions (FIST) for the past few years. A total of 459 science departments in
 various universities and other higher educational institutions have been given funds for strengthening the infrastructure in their
 teaching and research laboratories.
A high-level Committee has been constituted to draft an action plan for implementing the Recommendation contained in
 Science and Technology Policy 2003 in key areas like human resource development and basic research which would also include the
 existing S&T support system in the universities and other educational institutions.
Comments
The Committee appreciates the attempts made by CSIR for upgrading the S&T support system through various HRD schemes
 and hopes that the Recommendation contained in S&T policy 2003 will be implemented soon.

INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY & TECHNOLOGY MANAGEMENT (IP & TM)
Recommendation
The Committee commends the Department for emerging as a pioneering institute to achieve number one position in Indian &
 Foreign patent filings.  The Committee hopes that the Department would maintain its position.  Earlier Basmati rice was patented and
 some NGOs filed PILs in courts to activate the Government to take appropriate action.  The Committee hopes that CSIR will remain
 vigilant in future to safeguard our age-old indisputable rights to our traditional knowledge
(Para 30)
 
Action Taken by the Department
While acknowledging the appreciation received from the Committee, CSIR would continue to make efforts to remain at
 number one position in Indian and foreign patent filings and also try to retain its first position in PCT filings from developing
 countries.
In order to safeguard India’s undisputable rights in Traditional Knowledge, CSIR is contributing in major ways in developing
 Traditional Digital Library so  that it could be of use to Patent Examiners the world over. The digitalised information available on the
 internet would help them to examine the claim made by the applicant with respect to known traditional knowledge and then prevent
 them for granting wrong patents to the applicant on documented Traditional Knowledge of India as it already exists in public domain.
Additionally, CSIR is also making efforts to integrate Traditional Knowledge with Modern Knowledge and protect such
 inventive work nationally and internationally so as to safeguard Indian interests globally. CSIR has also developed and patented a
 method for fingerprinting of herbal formulation. Its use would help in checking on adulteration/poor quality and thus overcoming the
 problems of marketing substandard herbal materials.
Comments
The Committee notes with satisfaction the steps taken by CSIR with regard to patent and digital library.
R&D MANAGEMENT SUPPORT
Recommendation
The Committee observes that although CSIR initiates good works in various fields for the development of our country and
 indeed the mankind, these accomplishments have not been made known to the people.  It notes with satisfaction that efforts are being
 made to establish CSIR brand equity among the public.  To reach out to the people for making them aware of the important role
 played by CSIR, publicity through electronic and Print Media must be made.  Even the organization of exhibitions in rural areas
 displaying activities of the CSIR must be made for the benefit of our people.
(Para 34)
The Committee has been given to understand that due to personal efforts of one of its Members the Minister of Information &
 Broadcasting has approached the Minister of Science & Technology to find out as to how the Ministry of I&B could be of use to
 provide publicity for the scientific and technological programmes.  The Committee also understands that the Minister of I&B has also
 extended all cooperation in this regard.  The Committee therefore recommends that the Director General of CSIR must seize this
 opportunity and assist the Minister of Science & Technology in sending plans for giving wide publicity to its various programmes
 and activities.
(Para 34 A)
Action Taken by the Department
The awareness efforts have been given a boost during the Diamond Jubilee Year of the CSIR, when a large number of
 activities were taken up centrally as well as by each of the CSIR labs to make public aware about the scientific activities &
 achievements. Corporate advertisements by the CSIR HQrs. on important occasions, like Republic Day, Independence Day, National
 Technology Day, National Science Day, and days of importance to CSIR as a whole (Foundation Day, Bhatnagar Awards Function,
 World Patents Day, etc) were brought out by CSIR. More resources under publicity to enhance awareness activity are allocated. A
 short film on CSIR’s achievement was made and shown on the national channel of Doordarshan as a part of the live coverage of
 main function organized in Vigyan Bhavan, New Delhi, on the occasion of CSIR Diamond Jubilee, on 26 September 2002. Also, a
 country-wide awareness promotional programme is already launched during CSIR Diamond Jubilee year celebration, 52 places
 across the country have been identified where exhibition would be put up. These include the capitals of all states having CSIR
 laboratories/centres, and other important cities.  Efforts are being made at each place to publicise with a view to achieve the
 maximum possible participation of the local populace so as to realise maximum value from the efforts.
In the first place CSIR is endeavouring to develop necessary audio-visual software at CSIR. Already 20 themes have been
 selected on which CSIR proposes to prepare a five to seven minute film on each one of them. The film would address CSIR’s
 capabilities & services and depict its manifold activities.  Some of these activities relate to societal issues viz.: drugs for the poor,
 national water security, civil construction, and environment issues, rural industry, employment generation technologies. Other
 activities of the CSIR focusing attention on the technological prowess of CSIR will also be shown. Once the software is in place with
 the CSIR, efforts will be made to give wide spread publicity by utilising audiovisual media & help of the Ministry of Information &
 Broadcasting.

INFRASTRUCTURE RENOVATION & REFURBISHMENT
Recommendation
The Committee feels that the state-of-art infrastructure/laboratories are extremely important to further augment and enrich our
 capabilities in the fields of science and technology so as to face the increasing challenges thrown up by intense research activities in
 many scientific and technological institutions across the globe.  The infrastructure should be seen as a strategic national resource and
 funding should be given on a continuing basis to maximize their effectiveness, improvement & relevance for our scientific
 community.  The Infrastructure should also be developed keeping in view the future advances in science & engineering.  The
 Committee also feels that high speed internet access facility be established as vast amount of scientific data is available on the
 internet.  This will enable our scientists to have faster access to scientific data bases.
 (Para 38)
Action Taken by the Department
During the Tenth Plan, CSIR has initiated the scheme on Infrastructure Renovation & Refurbishment. It aims to renovate
 CSIR labs for various R&D programmes to enable them to undertake modern R&D activities. Through IT infrastructure renovation,
 it is proposed to connect all CSIR labs with LAN and internet connectivity on leased line – 2 Mbps. CSIR also has a plan to establish
 a Data Centre for secure e-enabled services and E-enabled MIS  application. For carrying networked R&D programmes the
 laboratories would be equipped with state of art IT facilities.
 
Comments
The Committee commends the efforts of the CSIR for renovating and refurbishing its infrastructure by extensively using
 information and communication technologies and hopes that the ongoing plans in this regard would be implemented soon.
 
TECHNOLOGY PROMOTION, DEVELOPMENT & UTILISATION PROGRAMME
Recommendation
The Committee feels that the merging of these programmes would not in any way effect the importance of these schemes and
 that they would continue to do the commendable work of transfer of technology for commercial exploitation.  The Committee also
 feels that such efforts of the CSIR would further encourage the entrepreneurship among our scientists and contribute towards
 technological self-reliance.  However the Committee recommends that greater attention must be paid by the DSIR to ensure that our
 industrial enterprises take necessary and important steps for augmenting their contributions to R&D.  Our expenditure for R&D as
 percentage of G.D.P. has fallen from 0.98 during 1958-59 to 0.8% during 21
st Century.  Out of it 80% is contributed by the
 government and only 20% comes from industry.  In almost all the developed countries contribution to R&D as percentage of GDP is
 3%.  Out of it industry contributes 80% and the government only 20%.  Our vision is to make India a developed country by the
 2020.  While the Committee strongly recommends that at least during the first quarter of the Tenth Five Year Plan contribution to
 R&D as percentage of GDP must target 1%  and the percentage contribution of industry to it must rise substantially.  In the age of
 innovation and competition, it is appropriately said  that “real temples of India have to be industry”.  For this to happen their
 contribution to R&D has to be bolstered.  Money spent in R&D is not an expenditure but an investment for the future.  It is also
 important that the know-how is sold to industry on competitive bids to extract the best return.
(Para 41)
Action Taken by the Department
The suggestion of the Committee to raise National R&D allocation to 1% of GDP is in tune with the S&T policy of the
 country. The Department continuously endeavours to encourage industry to enhance its cooperation, make use of fiscal incentives,
 announced by the Government from time-to-time and through other support measures for R&D.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.

Recommendation
The corporation continued to pursue the programme of Development and Promotion of Technologies appropriate for rural
 areas. The programme is aimed at bringing the key elements of innovation chain e.g. development on a carefully selected basis, of

The National Research Development Corporation has been promoting the various developed technologies indigenously

Recommendation
The Committee appreciates the efforts of the National Research Development Corporation in acting as a link between
 scientific laboratories and industrial establishments for transferring technologies.  However, the Committee feels that a lot needs to
 be done to reach out to our people living in rural areas.  In fact it is aptly said that rural areas are thirsting for Science & Technology.
 By developing appropriate technology for rural areas and transferring them for the benefit of our people a silent revolution can be
 ushered in for improving the living conditions of our teeming millions.
The Committee poignantly observed that we have yet to produce a prototype of a modern bullock cart for our farmers that
 could be more sturdy, far less strenuous for the bullock as well as passengers, distinctly faster & safer on roads.  Director General of

POLLUTION MONITORING MITIGATION SYSTEMS & DEVICES
Recommendation
The Committee feels that all pollution monitoring devices should be site specific as the causative agents in different areas are
 diverse and every anti pollution process must have measurable parameters to monitor its efficacy.  The Committee observes that
 pollution in the country has become acute and it is being seen as a challenge to the scientists to come up with new scientific tools to
 monitor and review the existing health based ambient quality standards.  The Committee observes that the department should
 coordinate with Pollution Control Boards in various states so that effective action is taken to sharply curb & finally prevent pollution
 in the country.
As far as the presence of arsenic content in water is concerned the Committee was informed that Bangladesh has developed
 some technology to rectify it.  The Committee recommends that CSIR may study that technology with a view to adopting it for our
 country’s benefit.
( Para 61)
Action Taken by the Department
The Central Pollution Control Board has the nodal responsibility to monitor and control pollution. They have informed that the
 present monitoring system does include assessment of water and ambient air quality.
For monitoring of water quality, 784 locations on rivers, lakes and ground water have been identified. In respect of ambient air
 quality monitoring, 290 locations in 94 cities/towns have been identified. The parameters being monitored for assessing the quality of
 water and ambient air are based on sources identified discharging waste into recipient environment. The devices used for monitoring
 are general and site specific as well. For example, for ambient air quality monitoring, high/low volume samplers are used for carrying
 out monitoring of criteria pollutants such as RSPM, SO
2 and NOx.
Special devices are used to monitor critical pollutants like VOC, PAH and BTX. To monitor the source emissions, from
 stationary sources (industries), stack monitoring devices and on-line monitors are used. However, devices used in the country for
 monitoring purposes are not completely indigenous and still number of devices are being imported. Efforts would be made to
 promote indigenous firms and institutions to manufacture equipment as per Indian conditions considering sites where monitoring are
 to be carried out and pollutants to be measured.
As far as CSIR is concerned, at NEERI all pollution monitoring devices are site specific & are being used substantially &
 extensively to identify and quantify pollution parameters of sources which are specific to sites: Antipollution process has certain
 measureable parameters which are determined by the regulatory authorities to monitor its efficacy. Pollution Control Boards are
 consulted in any pollution prevention and control assignment in the country taken by NEERI. It is true that the pollution levels in the
 country are increased and, NEERI is determining both ecotoxicity as well as genotoxicity of relevant pollutants in order to evolve
 health risk based ambient quality standards.
ITRC will coordiante with CPCB for manning use of bioremediation technologies developed as these have measurable
 parameters for monitoring their efficacy. CSIR has given a major thrust on the environmental health issues and ITRC has initiated a
 programme to develop new scientific tools for assessment of the genotoxicity. As observed by the Committee, it will intensify its
 efforts in this direction. As far as review of the health based ambient quality standards is concerned, information generated in this

ASTHMATIC & ALLERGIC DISORDERS MITIGATION MISSION
Recommendation
The Committee is pained to note that the percentage of Asthma patients of all ages has risen sharply.  It is assuming
 dimensions of a wide spread public health disaster.  There is a need to create awareness about the symptoms of the disease for early
 detection and cure.  The research should focus on the medicines, which are affordable to all classes in society.  The publicity of the
 medicine already discovered by the CSIR is grossly inadequate.  Special attention  needs to be focused on allergic Asthmas.
 (Para 65)
Action Taken by the Department
CSIR is focusing on Mission Mode Programme on Asthma. Research projects for developing early diagnosis and therapeutic
 modalities for asthma and allergic disorders are being undertaken. CSIR through one of its organisation (IICB) and the Institute of
 Genomics and Integrative Biology (IGIB), Delhi has initiated the following programmes to be carried out by several  CSIR
 laboratories.
(i)
                  Identifying and characterizing pollens which cause allergy and asthma for creating mass awareness;
(ii)                Studying the genetic and biochemical components of asthma. The polymorphisms in genes that are associated with
 asthma are being investigated. The biochemical properties of allergens are being studied;
(iii)               Using lung surfactant proteins (SP-A and SP-D) for developing therapeutic modalities for Allergen Broncho Pulmonary
 Aspergilosis (ABPA) disorder;
(iv)              Providing regular workshops to physicians from all over the country for better management of asthma and allergic
 disorders;
(v)                Preparing allergenic extracts for immunotherapy;
(vi)              Screening plant extract & extract of other sources (micro or insects) to identify new anti-microbial agents;
(vii)             Special projects have been given to identify new drug targets in M. Tuberculosis; and
(viii)           Identification of potential drug target using in silico approach.
In order to honour the Committee’s commitments relating to Asthma & ASMON, CSIR during the year has made ample
 publicity about ASMON – the herbal therapeutic of bronchial Asthma.  There has been a separate panel/poster on ASMON as a part
 of the CSIR Diamond Jubilee Exhibition and advertisement with the theme on ASMON is also being given at each venue of the

PARLIAMENT OF INDIA
file:///C/Users/user/Desktop/pri/Committee%20on%20S%20and%20T,%20Env.%20and%20Forests/120threport.htm[29-08-2018 16:28:55]
 exhibition in various parts of the country.  A large number of visitors to the exhibition with specific queries on ASMON are being
 helped with proper literature and addresses of the availability of the therapeutic at different places across the country.  A special
 advertisement was also published last year in the leading newspapers on the occasion of the World Asthma Day.
 
Comments
 The Committee commends the various initiatives and actions taken by the Department in combating various health hazards
 with special reference to ABPA disorders as well as creating awareness on Asthma and ASMON.
NEWER SCIENTIFIC HERBAL PREPARATIONS FOR GLOBAL POSITIONING
Recommendation
The Committee feels that intensive efforts should be made for acceptance of herbal medicines as complementary to modern
 mainstream medicines.  Besides, the committee feels that a regular watch has to be kept on those agencies who patent our traditional
 formulations and claim them as their own.  The Committee appreciates the observation of the Director General of CSIR who while
 replying to clarifications of members said that world wide attention is being focused on digital, herbal and spiritual ethos of which
 India has an abundant reserve.  The Committee entirely endorses the point that if our scientists apply themselves with dedication to
 harness these reserves twenty first century would be an Indian century. In fact Eric Hobsbwam in his book A New Century has
 written that India might surpass many other countries in the world and emerge as a  great country primarily because of the originality
 of her scientific and technological traditions which date back thousands and thousands of years.  At the same time the Committee
 feels that a check should be exercised on quacks in the healing profession specially those people who pose as doctors after having
 attained a degree in Ayurveda and misuse their positions to prescribe mainstream allopathic medicines or vice-versa.  The graduates
 in Ayurveda should be given the nomenclature of Ayurvedacharya & not doctor.
(Para 68)
Action Taken by the Department
CSIR through NISCAIR is already active in creation of a digital library in traditional knowledge, the project entitled
 Traditional Knowledge Digital Library (TKDL). It is a collaborative project between NISCAIR and Department of Indian System of
 Medicine and Homoeopathy, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and has been implemented at NISCAIR. About 36,000
 formulations mentioned in 14 authentic Ayurvedic texts listed out in Indian Drugs and Cosmetics Act have been transcribed in five
 international languages which are English, French, German, Spanish and Japanese. Images of the original Slokas, which have been
 transcribed, will also be included along with the references. The objective of creating TKDL is the defensive protection of traditional
 knowledge or in other words the database shall prevent the bio-piracy of traditional knoweldge. In all likelihood these database
 would act as a bridge between the codified traditional knowledge existing in Sanskrit and Hindi and the patent examiner at global
 level. It will serve as a non-patent online literature for use by the patent examiners. The transcription work on 36,000 formulations
 has been completed. However, the verification and validation work carried out by Eminent Ayurveda Experts is likely to be
 completed by August, 2003. Once validated the database will be available to patent examiners so as to prevent the misappropriation
 of the data use signing of the non-disclosure agareement by the patent offices and to prevent the misappropriation of the data.
The Department of Indian System of Medicine & Health has been requested to look into the concern of the Committee on
 quacks and also on graduates passing in Ayurveda for being given the nomenclature of Ayurvedacharya etc.
Comments
The efforts of the Department are commendable.
Recommendation
The Committee is heartened to note that the CSIR has entered into a strategic alliance with Arya Vaidya Sala and the Central
 Council of Research in Unani Medicine for revitalizing these ancient systems of medicines and making them relevant to our modern
 life and problems.  The Committee is satisfied to note that modern biological tools, techniques, processes and focused R&D are being
 applied to prepare herbal formulations.
The Committee discussed the severe handicap of Indian medicine systems which have to seek validation through western
 allopathic systems.  Evidently India, China & the orginators of Unani Systems of medicine have to fight together in all international
 fora including WHO.  The region specific systems of medicine get their validation from their ancient scriptures and if field trials
 establish their success they require to be validated all over the world on the basis of their conforming with their textual versions.  It is
 veritable  humiliation to the millennium old systems of ancient medicines to force them to pass the strait-jacket test systems of
 western pharmacology. Just as homeopathy has never had to pass through those validation procedures for getting world recognition
 as a valid system of medicine similarly validation of a system of medicine in India & China should get world recognition if they
 fulfill the conditions  laid down by the founders of their indigenous systems of medicines.  This calls for a concerted drive at world
 forums and the Committee recommends that CSIR is best suited to become the bulwark of this Campaign.
(Para 69)
Action Taken by the Department
CSIR has already started action with respect to the investigation and validation of the formulation selected on the basis of their
 past track record in ancient system of Medicine. CSIR in its 10
th Five Year Plan have initiated projects such as “Development of
 Newer scientific formulation for their global positioning”. These projects are being investigated using modern tools for the following

PARLIAMENT OF INDIA

 broad purposes.
(i)                  Establishing Mechanism of action;
(ii)                Validation of safety;
(iii)               Validation of efficacy
These investigations are pursued keeping in mind the strength of the formulations in ancient scriptures. Services of modern
 Clinicians, Molecular Biologists and Toxicologists are being involved besides ancient medicine practitioners. Keeping in view the
 above we also believe that CSIR is ideal organization to undertake the compaign as suggested.
We are thankful to the Committee that the initiative taken by CSIR for entering into agreement has been reconized as well as
 appreciated. CSIR is now trying to develop new herbal preparations. Indian System of Medicine is endowed with a wealth of
 knowledge created through observation, sustained practice and well conceived principles and while doing so it has taken into account
 the foundation and principles of health care enshrined in ancient Indian Scriptures wherein India propagated a holisitic vision of
 health carrying the Philosphy of health beyond the currently held vision of physical, mental and social well being. Realising this
 potential that India can become a player in discovering new therapautics for world health care on a sustained basis and also with a
 view to overcome the major constraints of funds and time required to discover modern drugs CSIR developed and followed special
 strategy based on India’s biodiversity and use of the knowledge base to develop new polyherbal preparations for treating not
 symptoms but specific disease. CSIR is thus partnering them to design & develop, new herbal formulations.  The basis of efficacy of
 these new herbal preparation would be their multiple action and synergy amongst various molecules.
Comments
The Committee notes with satisfaction the actions started by CSIR with regard to the Ancient Systems of Medicine, which are
 holistic and preventive.  It also notes with satisfaction that modern methods are being applied to these ancient systems to make them
 more effective.
DEVELOPING NEW GENERATION FUELS & LIBRICANTS
Recommendation
The Committee appreciates the Department for venturing into the development of new fuels.  The Committee feels that there is
 a need for adoption of wide variety of new generation alternative fuels as this would, apart from curbing the consumption of
 petroleum, help in reduction of pollution in our cities and towns.  The Committee would like the Department to develop fuels from
 waste matter and other non-bio-degradable substances which otherwise cause environmental degradations.
The Committee finds that similar research is being carried out by the Research & Development center of Indian oil
 Corporation at Faridabad.  It would be appropriate if the Department coordinated with them so as to prevent the duplication of
 research.
(Para 71)
Action Taken by the Department
The suggestion of the Committee is well taken. CSIR through its various laboratories and particularly through IIP has
 established close linkages with IOC(R&D). Such projects will be jointly coordinated in the area of new fuels particularly hydrogen &
 bio-fuels. R&D activities would also be focussed to develop fuels from wastes.
Comments
The Committee expresses its satisfaction with the reply and it would further like to see the redoubling of the efforts to produce
 alternative fuels so that the growing energy needs of the country can be met.  Assurances of the Department focus attention on R&D
 activities for development of fuels from waste products are encouraging.
SETTING UP A WORLD CLASS DRUG RESEARCH INSTITUTE
Recommendation
The Committee commends the challenging vision of the Department to set up a world-class drug research center. The
 Committee feels that the new center should aim at developing drugs for a wide range of diseases especially tuberculosis, Kala azar,
 AIDS, Hepatitis, Asthma by inter-alia intensive interaction with all varieties of Indian & Folk systems of medicine. Besides, the
 Committee feels that the new institute should go for manpower training and research to help pharmaceutical companies to improve
 the quality of their formulations. For example, in the budget for 2003-2004 government has given some incentives for Glucometers,
 but the prices of insulin are very high. Diabetes is spreading like an epidemic. India has been described as the future diabetic capital
 of the world. The Committee feels that the Department should make persistent efforts not only to produce insulin in our country by
 recombinant method so that its cost is reduced and it is made affordable for poor people, but also to create Ayurvedic cheaper
 formulations to treat diabetes for curing it and not just controlling it.
(Para 73)
Action Taken by the Department
Established in 1951 and committed to development of new drugs, pharmaceuticals and cost-effective process technologies
 against diseases prevalent in the country, CDRI made real impact in the Indian Health Care by developing a blood schizontocidal
 antimalarial marketed as E-mal; an antirelapse antimalarial as Aablaquin ; a non-steroidal oral contraceptive as Saheli and for use in
 dysfunctional uterine bleeding as Sevista and three economically viable process technologies for I-ephedrine, Dextropropoxyphene
 and a antimalarial Arteemether. Other significant achievements are a strong knowledgebase comprising 8000 research publications,
 more than 500 patents filed in India and abroad and about 1000 Ph.Ds spread over the Academic and Pharmaceutical sector nation-

PARLIAMENT OF INDIA

wide holding prestigious positions in the best multinational pharma companies.
New drug discovery research and development being a multifaceted and multidisciplinary activity, the institute has since been
 actively involved in various research activities ranging from understanding of host-pathogen interactions, identification of new
 targets and designing bioassays rational drug design mechanism of action and admetox profiling of new drug molecules for
 development of safe and effective drugs. This has led the institute to acquire expertise, infrastructure and a strong knowledgebase not
 only to work in areas of current thrust but also take-up challenging problems likely to affect developing countries especially India in
 near future.
The suggestions/observations put forth by the expert Committee in the above report have been given due consideration to a
 major extent not only in the vision document prepared in respect of ‘Setting-up a world-class drug research Institute’ at Sitapur Road,
 Lucknow, but have also been incorporated in the on-going R&D programs at the Central Drug Research Institute, Lucknow.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and hopes that adequate efforts would be made in making cheaper medicines using indigenous
 systems.
DEVELOPING NEW BUILDING CONSTRUCTION MATERIALS
Recommendation
The Committee is of the opinion that new construction materials should be less energy intensive for building economical
 dwelling units for millions of our people. As large parts of our country live in villages, locally available material may be used to
 produce technologies for construction of houses & the technologies need to be region-specific.
(Para 75)
Action Taken by the Department
Building materials and technologies developed by Central Building Research Institute (CBRI) for construction of houses and
 other buildings is based on  use of locally available materials and manpower with low energy consumptions.  These Technologies are
 relevant to different geo-climatic regions of the country depending upon the availability of materials and skills of the region.  As
 desired by the Committee, under a new network programme of CSIR, full cognizance of the energy and use of local materials has
 been taken.  The major objective of the project is the development and application of low alternative/new building construction
 materials from conceptual to commercialisation through use of energy efficient and environment friendly building materials
 processes and construction technologies with emphasis on value addition to agro industrial wastes for sustainable development.  The
 project envisage to provide materials for building economical dwelling units to cater to the masses in difficult regions of the country.
Comments
The Committee observes with satisfaction the fact that building materials and technology developed at CBRI takes into
 account the different geo-climatic regions and different local needs.
INFECTIOUS DISEASED HANDLING STORAGE & RESEARCH FACILITIES
Recommendation
The Committee feels that the new storage and handling facilities should be of world-class standard. The Committee hopes that
 this facility would conduct basic research for controlling infectious diseases to reduce the risk of morbidity. The Committee hopes that
 the Department would conduct periodic review of such facilities to properly maintain their standards. The Committee emphasizes the
 need for adopting measurable parameters for effective monitoring of the progress being made in this direction.
(Para 79)
Action Taken by the Department
CSIR has been at the fore front of finding new diagnostics and therapeutic methods for controlling infectious organism and
 disease caused by them. CSIR is initiating a programme during the Tenth Plan to create adequate infrastructural storage & handling
 facility in number of CSIR laboratories. These facilities once created would enable CSIR for implementation of appropriate safety
 guidelines and enhance the speed of ongoing basic research carried on infectious microorganism at these facilities to be accelerated
 through networking.
Comments
The Committee is satisfied that the methods and techniques devised by the department to control and eliminate various
 infectious diseases are of immense significance and beneficial to the masses.  It further suggests that the Department should take
 utmost care for the maintenance of laboratories and promotion of basic research.
GIVING SPECIAL AWARDS TO THE UNEDUCATED PEOPLE WHO DISPLAY THEIR GENIUS IN SCIENTIFIC FIELD
Recommendation
The Committee observes that innovative ideas on scientific aspects not only come from urban educated people but also from
 persons who are not educated and who hail from rural areas.  Scientific discovery of excellence gives rise to technological innovations
 of excellence.  The Committee therefore recommends that the Department should create special awards for the uneducated people
 who apply their genius in scientific fields and make important discoveries.  There is also need for publicity about the quality testing
 facility so that people at large avail of it.
(Para 86)

Action Taken by the Department
Department is operating a scheme known as Technopreneur Promotion Programme (Tepp) essentially to tap the vast
 innovative potential of the citizen of India. It promotes individual innovators to become technology based entrepreneurs. Through
 Tepp financial support to individual innovators irrespective of whether they are educated or not but having original ideas is provided
 to convert their ideas to working models/prototypes etc. So far four inventors who were farmers, artisans were supported for their
 products. Department is bringing out hand out and brochures providing information on the quality testing facilities available at
 various National Laboratories with a view to making organisations aware of the facilities.
Comments
 The Committee notes the reply and would like to see more programmes in the lines of Techno Promotion Programme (Tepp),
 to encourage and nurture the innovative potential of the individual entrepreneurs in the country.
NATIONAL SCIECNE & TECHNOLOGY HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT
Recommendation
The Committee feels that the amount is not at all enough for developing human resources for science and technology and
 therefore recommends that substantively higher allocations must be made for the above scheme.
Interest and awareness among students for science and technology has to be sustained. The Committee feels that, Science
 Cafes, in the pattern of Cyber Cafes, may be opened in different localities and educational institutions. Exposure to scientific works
 and activities in such cafes would encourage the youth of our country to show more interest in science. The Committee strongly
 recommends that some time (at least five minutes) may be allocated in the chaupal programme of Doordarshan to show the activities
 of CSIR for promoting people’s awareness about them. The Ministry of I&B has already indicated its enthusiastic willingness to
 provide all help in this direction. The Committee would like to know the quantifiable impact that the scholarship scheme has
 produced. It is hoped that individual record of progress of scholarship holders is being maintained & there is provision to terminate
 the scholarships of indifferent students. If there is no such specific mechanism in place, it would be desirable to introduce one. That
 alone will ensure optimum, benefit from the investment made.
(Para 89)
Action Taken by the Department
The Department would take up the matter at RE stage with the Ministry of Finance and request them to consider enhancement
 in the budgetary support to the scheme on S&T human resource development.  In the mean time the department is working out the
 exact requirement to meet the shortfall.
In the Tenth Plan, CSIR under the scheme on S&T Human Resource Development, has planned to adopt school & colleges to
 raise the standard of science teaching.  The suggestion of the Committee to open science  cafe is accordingly being considered to be
 dovetailed in the scheme.
CSIR is happy to inform that the scholar scheme which has been in operation since 1950 & 1983 has so far supported about
 90,000 JRF, SRF, Research Associates & Senior Research Associates. These scholars have published quality papers in Science
 Citation Index Journals and thus been able to contribute in generation of new  knowledge.
Checks & balances have been built in.  The progress of these fellows are evaluated and monitored every year through peer
 reviews. Rigorous monitoring is also undertaken at the end of two years while the fellows are considered for upgradation.
Comments 
The Committee notes the reply with satisfaction and hopes that vigorous efforts would be undertaken to create quality human
 resources in the fields of science and technology.

R E P O R T
The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Ministry of Environment & Forests on the
 recommendations contained in the One Hundred-twelfth Report of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee
 on Science & Technology, Environment & Forests on the Demands for Grants (2003-2004) of the Ministry of Environment &
 Forests which was presented/laid to both Houses of Parliament on 2

 contained in One Hundred-twelfth Report of the Committee. Action Taken notes on the recommendations of the Committee
 were received from the Department on 29

The Committee’s recommendations, action taken thereon and comments of the Committee on the action taken by the
 Ministry of Environment & Forests are set out in the succeeding paragraphs: -
REASONS FOR SHORTFALL IN OUTLAYS AND UTILISATION
Recommendation
          The Committee recommends that at R.E. stage curtailment of funds for the Ministry may be avoided so as to enable the
 smooth and unhindered implementation of programmes and policies of  the Ministry. The Committee also recommends that the
 programmes and policies may be effectively and substantially implemented at the ground level so as to get the desired result.
(Para 7)
Action Taken by the Ministry
This has been the constant endeavour of the Ministry to achieve 100% utilization of plan funds and to ensure effective
 implementation of various schemes and programmes.
A stringent review mechanism has been put in place where by the Secretary (E&F) reviews progress of plan expenditure
 every week.   The institution of the nodal officers from the Ministry for each state has helped to bring in coordinated efforts
 with the State Governments.
Ministry also makes efforts to obviate any cut in plan allocation at RE stage. However, the final decision rests with the
 Ministry of Finance and they take into account several factors such as overall availability of financial resources, competing
 demands of the various Ministries/Departments, the requirements of the different State Governments etc.  However a copy of
 the recommendations is being forwarded to Ministry of Finance for appropriate action.
Comments
The Committee is not satisfied with the reply and observes that there is an urgent need to review the whole planning and
 budgetary process in the Ministry effectively so that realistic physical and financial targets are projected in the budget and
 planned projects are not hampered due to drastic cut at R.E. stage. The Ministry should also take up the matter seriously with
 the Ministry of Finance not to reduce the budgetary allocation at R.E. stage.
ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION OF TAJ MAHAL
Recommendation
The protection of the Taj Mahal has been a major priority and constant efforts are required to save the monument. The
 Committee feels that concerted effort should be taken for the protection of the Taj which suffered substantial damage due to
 pollution. The Committee recommends that instead of involving multiple agencies for the protection of Taj, a constituent body
 be formed which would be responsible for coordination with all allied agencies, supported by a strong legal framework for
 effective implementation of the policies undertaken.

 progress of  implementation of various schemes for protection of the Taj Mahal and conservation and improvement of the

 Secretary (U.P.) is monitoring the programme of implementation of projects in the TTZ area.
Comments
            While the Committee notes the reply, it appears that all efforts of the Ministry fails to make any significant improvement
 in the protection of Taj Mahal from environmental hazard.
NATIONAL RIVER CONSERVATION PLAN INCLUDING GANGA ACTION PLAN
Recommendation
The Committee observes that for any plan or programme regarding cleaning of rivers of such a magnitude as Ganga, to
 succeed, it is necessary to have a meticulous planning. Any delay in its execution is bound to result in the plan going awry.
 More so, because the parameters regarding the size of the population and the extent of urbanization etc., which would have
 been taken into account at the stage of planning, are subject to rapid changes in a country like India. Hence, timely execution is
 crucial for such programmes or else we would suffer severe consequences of contamination of our rivers on  the  banks of
 which our civilization began and flourished.
(Para 22
)
Action Taken by the Ministry
These observations are being taken into account and noted for compliance. The parameters regarding size of population
 & extent of urbanization are in-built in the detailed project reports (DPR) submitted by the State Govts.   The design parameters
 of the facilities take into account the future projections of population and pollution load etc.   The notable achievements of
 National River Conservation Plan are as under :
Of the 261 schemes sanctioned, 259 schemes have completed in 25 towns of  Uttaranchal, U.P, Bihar & West Bengal at a
 cost of Rs. 452 crore under GAP Phase-I.
Of the 35 Sewage Treatment Plants (STP), 33 STPs having a capacity of  865 million litres per day (MLD) have been set
 up under GAP Phase-I.
Length of polluted river stretch reduced from 740 kms. to 437 kms between Rishikesh (U.P) & Rajmahal (Bihar) due to
 implementation of GAP Phase-I.
The water quality results of River Ganga at polluted stretches namely Kanpur, Allahabad,  Varanasi, Patna indicate  a
 decreasing trend of pollution levels from 1986 to 2002.
Of the 33 Sewage Treatment Plants, 29 STPs having a capacity of  738 MLD have been set up under YAP Phase-I.
252 schemes have been completed in 21 towns of  Haryana, Delhi & U.P at a cost of  Rs. 680.10 crore, with Rs. 660.06
 crore assistance coming from Japan Bank for International Co-operation (JBIC).
A Cost Benefit Analysis of GAP Phase-I  carried out by Harvard Institute of  International Development indicated that in
 terms of  both the time taken and cost involved, GAP compares favorably with those of  other major rivers of the world like
 Thames, Rhine & Danube.
Comments
            The Committee notes the reply and desires that a copy of the report of the Harvard Institute of International Development
 may be supplied to the Committee. The Committee notes that mere establishment of Sewage Treatment Plants is not enough.
 They have to function round the year. It has been observed that in the absence of adequate power supply, the plants do not
 function. Therefore, the Committee had recommended for the establishment of generator sets in these plants.

Recommendation
The  Committee is constrained to observe that even after nearly two decades of Ganga Action Plan (GAP)-I, the

 implement such plans.
(Para 23)

YAMUNA ACTION PLAN
Recommendation
The Committee is deeply perturbed to note that the Yamuna water at Delhi continues to be stinking and dirty. It notes
 with concern that waste  is still dumped in the Yamuna river through drains. The Committee notes with anxiety that cleaning  of
 sewerage has become erratic and the functioning of the sewage treatment plants have been stalled due to frequent power cuts or
 some other reason. These STPs cannot afford to be dysfunctional for even a minute and the Committee would like to know  the
 arrangements for captive gensets. It also noted with concern about the lack of public awareness and public participation in the
 cleaning of rivers. The Committee is, therefore, of the view that the cleansing  of Yamuna has to go beyond cosmetic  measures
 like removal of slums along the banks and greening of banks. Perhaps the more concrete  solution is to prevent the drainage
 wastes from entering the river and to ensure the increase of the flow of fresh water.  The Committee would also like to  know if
 the Delhi Government/Central Government have obtained an extension of time from the Supreme Court for compliance of its
 order which was to be implemented by 31.3.2003 or are the Governments responsible for non-compliance, therefore,
 committing contempt of the Supreme Court.
(Para 34)
Action taken by the Ministry
            Yamuna Action Plan has been  implemented in Delhi  at a cost of Rs. 180 crore, (where only 2 sewage treatment plants,
 each of 10 million litres per day (mld) capacity, 4 mini sewage treatment plants, and  10 micro sewage treatment plants of a
 total capacity of 10 mld were  constructed besides about 960 community toilet complexes).  However, the expected level of
 improvement in river water quality is yet to be achieved.  GOI had posed a project of YAP –II at an estimated cost of Rs. 2000
 crore to JBIC. But due to constraint of resources, JBIC has committed an assistance of Rs. 624 crore (for Delhi, Haryana and
 UP out of which Rs. 387 crore is for Delhi).  The major  focus under YAP-II shall be on sewerage works in Delhi.   While a
 capacity to treat 135 mld of sewage will be created, 624 mld of sewage treatment capacity is to be rehabilitated. Out of 91 km.
 of trunk sewer which is defunct due to settlement/siltation, 30 km. is proposed  to be rehabilitated under this project.  In
 addition, YAP-II will also address the programme of capacity building of implementing agencies.  Public participation  and
 water quality management programme to assess the efficacy of the project will receive a special focus.   The works under YAP-
II are envisaged to take a completion period of  5 years to be completed by September, 2008. 
In addition, Government of Delhi is also implementing projects for abatement of pollution of river Yamuna in Delhi
 through their own resources.  An amount of Rs. 630 crore has been spent by Government of Delhi on these projects during the
 IX Plan. Government of Delhi is constructing 15 CETPs in 21 industrial estates to create a capacity of 180 mld.   The STPs  
 constructed by Delhi Jal Board are being provided with captive power generation sets in future.   Remaining works proposed to
 be executed for abatement of pollution of river Yamuna are envisaged to be taken up under YAP Phase-III.
10 cumecs of fresh water is to be released by the riparian states as per directions of the Supreme Court for augmentation
 of flow of water in the river at Delhi.  Central Water Commission is monitoring the release of the fresh water by the respective

 quality to the desired level by 31.3.2005.

FOREST CONSERVATION, DEVELOPMENT AND REGENERATION
Recommendation
In view of the steady depletion of forest resources and increasing deforestation, the Committee is of the view that the
 active and willing participation of local communities is necessary for the success of any forest regeneration programme.  In the
 absence of any direct benefit and sufficient authority for the local community, there would be very little incentive for them to
 participate in any  activity of the Ministry. Therefore, the Committee recommends that the Joint Forest Management (JFM) 
 programme should be vigorously pursued by involving women and tribals to protect and regenerate degraded forests. Moreover
 non-timber forest produce should also be properly regenerated, harvested, processed and marketed for improving the economy
 of forest-dwellers.
      (Para 53)
Action taken by the Ministry
The steady depeletion of forest resources is being tackled through National Afforestation Programme (NAP), A central
 Sector Scheme being implemented by the Ministry.  NAEB is the Nodal Agency for the implementation of this Programme. 
 The implementation of NAP is through the decentralized set up of Forest Development Agencies (FDAs), which are Federation
 of  Joint Forest Management Committees.  NAP, therefore is indirectly promoting the policy of Joint Forest Management
 through FDAs.  However, the availability of funds under the National Afforestation Programme is a major limiting factor in
 eliciting JFMC’s greater participation under the Programme.
In accordance with the National Forest Policy, 1988, Ministry of Environment & Forests is vigorously pursuing the
 involvement of communities in regeneration of degraded forests through Joint Forest Management (JFM) programme on care
 and share principle.  In this regard, the Ministry of Environment & Forests continuously liaise with the State Governments on
 this matter and had also issued guidelines from time to time to empower the committees and also to make this programme a
 success.  The guidelines issued in February 2000 emphasize the meaningful participation of women in JFM.  It clearly states
 that at least 50% members of the General Body should be women and in the Executive Committee, it should be 33%.  These
 guidelines envisage involvement of people including tribal to protect and regenerate the forests including non-timber forest
 produce.  So far more than 72,000 JFM Committees have been constituted in the country for the protection and regeneration of
 degraded forests.  In order to involve the people in planning and decision making process, Forest Development Agencies
 (FDAs) are being constituted in all the States.  These FDAs are the confederation of Joint Forest Management Committees and
 are empowered to take decision on regeneration of forests, choice of species and other employment generation activities.  The
 Ministry on 24
th December 2002 further issued the guidelines on empowerment, transparency, proper regeneration, marketing,
 and value addition for Non Timber Forest Produce so that the collector and gatherer of the NTFPs get maximum return on their
 products.

            The Committee notes the reply.

FOREST CONSERVATION, DEVELOPMENT AND REGENERATION
Recommendation
The Committee was given to  understand that one of the goals of the Ministry is to increase the forest cover of the
 country upto 25%  by 2007  and 33% by 2012. The Committee appreciates the goal set out by the Ministry but is of the view
 that a blanket approach should not be adopted in this regard. Some States already have a forest cover in excess of 33% and
 complain about hampering of development activities due to thick forest cover. Therefore, the policy of increasing forest cover
 should be implemented only in those states which are short of the stipulated target so that a balanced proportion of forest cover 
 can be maintained in all parts of the country.
(Para 55)
 
Action taken by the Ministry
This recommendation of the Committee has a policy dimension.  As far as Ministry is concerned it is clarified that the
 afforestation programame is being taken up only in the degraded forest areas and fringe villages.  Therefore the quality of the
 forest and in turn the forest is being improved within the recorded forest area only, which otherwise cannot be diverted for
 development works without the approval of the competent authority under the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980.
            The productive and protective nature of forests transcends geographical boundaries.  In order to maintain this nature of
 forests, one of the most important goals of the Ministry is to increase the forest cover of the country upto 25% by 2007 and 33%
 by 2012.  The developmental activities in any state are not hampered because of the thick forest cover.  The diversion of forest
 land for non-forestry activities under Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980, for various developmental projects like Power,
 Irrigation, Drinking water supply, Roads, Railway Lines etc. is considered on the merits of the case. India is committed to the
 concept of sustainable management of its forest resources and tree wealth.  The proportion of the country’s geographical area
 under forest/tree cover is one of the basic criteria to judge sustainability. The National Forest Policy, 1988 envisages that
 national goal should be to have a minimum of one third of total land area of the country under forest/tree cover. In the hills and
 in the mountainous region, the aim should be to maintain two third of the area under such cover in order to prevent erosion and
 land degradation and ensure the stability of the fragile ecosystem.
            Forest is on the Concurrent List of the Constitution. It is true that the forest cover in some of the states is more than
 national goal, but the national goal has not been achieved so far. The Ministry of Environment & Forests is trying to achieve the
 national goal enshrined in the National Forest Policy, 1988 in a holistic way with a full support to the forest rich states by
 assisting them in strengthening the institutional framework like Joint Forest Management Committees, Forest Development
 Agencies and funding through various centrally sponsored schemes. Simultaneously, efforts are being made on promoting tree
 plantation both outside and inside the forest areas in those states which are deficient in forest/tree cover.  The efforts are being
 made on both the forest rich and deficient states, as we have to take a holistic picture at the national level. While the focus has

Recommendation
The Committee notes that active involvement  of people in the development of the forestry sector has to be further

NATIONAL LAKE CONSERVATION PLAN
Recommendation
The Committee is  perturbed to note that a big project which could play a significant role in restoring the environmental
 health of the country is suffering due to apathy and the lackadaisical attitude of the Central and State Governments. It was
 started in 1994, but little seems to have been done for cleaning of lakes and a lot of  time has been spent either in finalizing
 contracts or preparing action plans or discussing cost factors.  The Committee feels that lakes are critical in sustaining the
 environmental health of our cities. Acting as a huge reservoir, they not only provide water but also recharge and replenish the
 ground water. Lakes also play an important role in preventing floods. Besides, their importance from the point of view of
 beauty, and aesthetics are well acclaimed. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry come out with a
 comprehensive approach and execute all its programmes with seriousness and commitment. Otherwise our lakes will very soon
 be garbage dumps. When lakes dry up during continuous droughts like in Rajasthan today it is suggested that programme for
 desilting and deepening of the bed of those lakes needs to be taken up on a war footing, if necessary with the help of Army
 Engineering Corps.
(Para 64)
Action taken by the Ministry
            The National Lake Conservation Plan (NLCP) was conceptualized in 1994.  After obtaining the pre-feasibility reports
 from the State Governments for 10 identified lakes, the NLCP was posed for approval  by the Cabinet Committee.  The
 Ministry was however, directed to seek external assistance.  No external funding agency evinced any interest.  The Government
 of  India’s approval to lake conservation was accorded in June, 2001.  Since then 22 lakes have already been approved for
 taking up conservation measure at an estimated cost of  about  Rs. 137 crore.  So far an expenditure of Rs.1.90 crore has been
 incurred on NLCP.  The site specific conservation measures include sewage diversion and treatment, desilting, deweeding,
 insitu lake conservation measures like bioremediation on constructed wetland, lake beautification and lake front development,
 low cost sanitation, public participation etc.
The scope of work under NLCP has been enlarged during the X Plan by including conservation of rural lakes along with
 urban lakes.  All State Governments have been asked to prioritise and send proposals for lakes in their States.  Depending upon
 the pollution status and the availability of funds, these shall be included under NLCP.  During the last meeting of  NRCA held

BIO-MEDICAL WASTE MANAGEMENT
Recommendation
      The Committee feels that the scientific management of medical waste is being  dangerously neglected in the country. The
 staff charged with the responsibility for sanitation and cleanliness in hospitals and other medical units seem to be ignorant of
 the regulations for Bio-medical waste (BMW) disposal. Hoards of broken needles, soiled cotton  and bandages, laboratory
 tested blood/urine/stood samples, leftover plaster of Paris coats, abandoned organs, used utensils, instruments and containers
 lying right in the precincts of hospitals have been noticed by people. Even these wastes have been shown to the M.Ps. The
 Committee observes that in some parts of the country many incinerators installed to dispose of medical waste are dysfunctional.
 In U.P. alone out of 33 incinerators, 31 are not functioning. The Committee recommends that responsibility has to be fixed for
 the negligence which cause such a state of affairs and deterrent action taken against the officers responsible for the running of
 incinerators. The Committee, therefore, recommends that  persons in small and big nursing homes and all hospitals heed to be
 trained regarding this aspect. A  capsule one or two day course  should be run each month in all leading Government hospitals
 of the country and not only staff but the hospital  in-charge must also be  made to attend these courses at the end of which
 proper certificate should also be awarded  to trainees. Taking into account the mushrooming growth of nursing homes the
 Committee recommends that a proposal may  be considered to link the opening of nursing homes with their capacity to treat
 and manage biomedical wastes. Medical waste management cannot be left only to the Municipalities. Open discussions should
 also be held among technical experts people’s  representatives and representatives of hospitals and nursing homes for evolving
 a strategy and method for proper disposal of BMW. In addition to these measures, a recycling industry bases on hospital waste
 needs to be dealt with in an exemplary fashion.

The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Department of Biotechnology on the Recommendations
 contained in the One Hundred-sixteenth Report of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science &
 Technology, Environment & Forests on the Demands for Grants (2003-2004) of the Department of Biotechnology which was

 Hundred- sixteenth Report of the Committee. Action Taken notes on the Recommendations of the Committee were received
 from the Department on 30
th July, 2003.
The Committee’s Recommendation, action taken thereon and comments of the Committee on the action taken by the
 Department of Scientific and Industrial Research are set out in the succeeding paragraphs: -
Recommendation
            The Committee was informed that one of the recurring problems of the Department is the shortfall of the non-plan
 budget.  Recurrence of such problems on year to year basis, the committee was apprised, has created a compelling situation for
 the autonomous bodies whereby they had to cut down from plan funds to pay salaries to the scientists.  The Committee is
 constrained to note that scientific institutions engaged in research in frontier areas of science have to confront such a situation. 
 The additional requirement of the Department of non-plan expenditure is to the tune of Rs.5.00 crores.  The Committee,
 therefore, recommends that sufficient funds may be provided to the Department to overcome this problem.  It further underlines
 that the Departments dealing with science and technology should be accorded priority for allocation of funds and if necessary,
 special provisions may be made for them so that they do not face such problems.  Biotechnology era is waiting to dominate the
 World economy in the next twenty years.  Investment in this field is not commensurate with the potential of this branch of
 Science.
(Para 8)
Action taken by the Department
The Department has corresponded with Ministry of Finance, Government of India, on additional non-plan requirement as
 per recommendations. The matter is being pursued.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and hopes that the Department will pursue the Ministry of Finance to take cognizance of
 the matter.
HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT
Recommendation
The Committee recommends the Department to accord high priority to the issue of Human Resource Development and
 should coordinate with the University Grants Commission to implement the programme all over the country.
(Para 16)
Action taken by the Department
The Human Resource Development programme has been accorded high priority by the department. The department has
 decided to start new courses in the specialized subject areas of biotechnology in different parts of the country. For the first time
 model syllabi has been published for the post graduate courses in general biotechnology, medical biotechnology, agriculture
 biotechnology, animal biotechnology and M.Tech in biochemical engineering and biotechnology and circulated to University
 Grant Commission (UGC), Ministry of Human Resource Development (MHRD), All India Council for Technical Education
 (AICTE), Universities/ institutions who are implementing post graduate teaching courses supported by the department as well
 as other universities for implementation from the academic session 2003-04. It is also proposed to start Ph. D fellowship

Recommendation
The Committee is of the view that efforts should be made to make use of the tissue culture and floriculture technology in
